subclassFeature.name: Travel Agent
entries: {@i "The perfect Paradiso is always one journey away."}

The world is filled with places claiming to be Paradise, from tranquil beaches and enchanted forests to cities where knowing where to eat and where to shop is practically a survival skill. Those who decide to experience these places for themselves, wandering through dark woods, descending through infernal circles, climbing mountains that seem impossible to traverse, and continuing upward among the stars, are Travel Agents. Of course, they carefully note which destinations defined their travels and which deserve a return visit.

entries.name: Travel Advisory
entries: Usually recognized by an overfilled journal, several unnecessary maps, and strong opinions regarding local accommodations and what counts as the local delicacy, Travel Agents roam in search of the perfect getaway; for themselves, their companions, or any clients brave enough to follow. They are dependable guides and enthusiastic planners, but they rarely remain anywhere for long, certain that their Paradiso awaits somewhere along the next journey.

subclassFeature.name: Travelogue
entries: You maintain a collection of destinations you've discovered during your travels, called your Travelogue. Choose two locations you visited before becoming a Travel Agent, and assign one environment from the Travel Agent Environments table to each.

After spending at least 8 hours traveling through or exploring a distinct location, you can register the location in your Travelogue when you finish a long rest there. When you register a location, record its name and general position, and assign it one environment from the Travel Agent Environments table that appropriately describes it. The DM determines whether a location is sufficiently distinct to be registered and whether your chosen environment is appropriate.

There is no limit to the number of locations you can register. A location can't be registered more than once, and registering multiple locations with the same environment doesn't grant additional copies of that environment's benefits.

You accurately recall the appearance and general layout of each registered location, as well as the route by which you first reached it in relation to other locations in your Travelogue. While on the same plane of existence as a registered location, you know its approximate direction and distance from you.

subclassFeature.name: Featured Destination
entries: When you finish a long rest, you can choose one location recorded in your Travelogue to be your Featured Destination. The location remains your Featured Destination until you choose another recorded location when you finish a long rest.
While a location is your Featured Destination, you gain the Amenity and Excursion provided by its Destination Profile, and it determines the damage type of your Local Specialty.

You can use an Excursion a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded up. You regain one expended use when you finish a short rest and all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
If an Excursion requires a saving throw, the saving throw DC equals your ranger spell save DC. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for any spell you cast through an Excursion.

subclassFeature.name: Local Specialty
entries: You learn to draw upon the distinctive qualities of your Featured Destination in battle. Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can deal an extra {@dice 1d6} damage to the target. The damage type is determined by the Destination Profile of your Featured Destination, and is considered magical for the purposes of overcoming resistances.
When you reach 11th level in this class, the extra damage increases to {@dice 2d6}.

subclassFeature.name: On-Site Expertise
entries: While you are within a location recorded in your Travelogue, you gain the Amenity provided by that location's Destination Profile in addition to the Amenity of your Featured Destination. You can also use either Destination Profile's Excursion, but both draw from the same number of Excursion uses.
Being within a recorded location doesn't change the damage type of your Local Specialty. If the location and your Featured Destination provide the same Amenity, you gain that Amenity only once.

subclassFeature.name: Group Package
entries: When you finish a long rest, choose a number of willing creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one creature). Until you finish your next long rest, each chosen creature gains the Amenity provided by your Featured Destination while it is within 30 feet of you, you aren't {@condition incapacitated}, and it can see or hear you.
A creature benefiting from this feature doesn't gain the Amenity granted to you by On-Site Expertise.

subclassFeature.name: Return Ticket
entries: You can lead your clients directly to the destination promised in your itinerary. You can spend 10 minutes consulting your Travelogue and preparing your traveling companions. At the end of that time, you and up to eight willing creatures of your choice within 30 feet of you teleport to your Featured Destination.
Each creature arrives in an unoccupied space chosen by the DM at or as close as possible to the location recorded in your Travelogue.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Alchemical Engineer
entries: An Alchemical Engineer does not consider a transmutation complete merely because it produces the intended result. Alchemical Engineers study successful reactions until they can be replicated with enough precision to manufacture their effects en masse.

Their Transmutation Engines carry the prime atom, Salt, through articulated arms and carefully positioned glyphs, transforming it into stable products. Some pursue the vital elements and Quintessence, while others refine Lead toward Gold through experimental metallurgy.

entries.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency with alchemist’s supplies. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of artisan’s tools of your choice.

entries.name: Alchemical Engineer Spells
entries: You always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Alchemical Engineer Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don’t count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

entries.name: Transmutation Engine
entries: You construct a Transmutation Engine, a Tiny magical mechanism containing articulated arms, tracks, and alchemical glyphs. The engine can be worn, carried in one hand, or attached to an object you are carrying.
You can use the engine as a spellcasting focus for your artificer spells. When you do so, you must have a free hand to manipulate it.

If the engine is lost or destroyed, you can create a replacement over the course of 1 hour using alchemist’s supplies and 50 gp worth of metal and other raw materials, which the process consumes. This work can be performed during a short or long rest.

entries.name: Atoms
entries: Your engine can contain a number of alchemical atoms equal to your proficiency bonus. Each atom occupies one space within this capacity, regardless of its type.
When you finish a long rest, every atom within the engine becomes Salt, and the engine produces enough additional Salt atoms to reach its maximum capacity.

An atom removed from the engine is inert unless it is placed within one of your Infusions. An atom that is expended remains unavailable until a feature returns it to Salt or until you finish a long rest.
Your Transmutation Die is a d6. It is used by several of your Bonding effects and later changes according to the metal within your engine.

entries.name: Glyph of Duplication
entries: Once during each of your turns, when you cast an artificer spell associated with one of the effects shown in the Elemental Duplication table, you can convert one Salt atom within the engine into the corresponding classical element.

The spell need not damage a creature for this conversion to occur. If the spell is associated with more than one element, you choose which atom is created. The new atom remains within the engine until used.

entries.caption: Elemental Duplication
rows: Cold damage or the restoration of hit points

entries.name: Glyph of Bonding
entries: As a bonus action, you can bond one atom within the engine to a creature you can see within 60 feet of you. The atom produces the corresponding effect below. If an effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals your artificer spell save DC.

items.name: Salt 🜔.
items.entry: The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or become {@condition restrained} by a growth of crystallized Salt until the start of your next turn. The Salt atom is expended.

items.name: Air 🜁.
items.entry: Move the target in any direction, up to 5 feet. An unwilling creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw to resist this movement. This movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks.

items.name: Earth 🜃.
items.entry: The target gains temporary hit points equal to one roll of your Transmutation Die plus your Intelligence modifier and can’t be moved against its will until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Fire 🜂.
items.entry: The target must make a Dexterity saving throw. It takes fire damage equal to one roll of your Transmutation Die plus your Intelligence modifier on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

items.name: Water 🜄.
items.entry: The first time the target takes damage before the start of your next turn, reduce that damage by one roll of your Transmutation Die plus your Intelligence modifier.

entries: After an Air, Earth, Fire, or Water atom produces its effect, it returns to the engine as Salt. Other types of atoms are expended unless their descriptions say otherwise.

entries.name: Atom Infusions
entries: The following Infusions are available to an artificer who has the Transmutation Engine feature.
Each of these Infusions functions normally whether or not it contains an atom. An item’s Infused (Atom) property can be used only while the item contains the atom named in that property.

entries.name: Loading an Atom
entries: As a bonus action while touching an item bearing one of these Infusions, you can transfer the atom required by that Infusion from your Transmutation Engine into the item. An item can contain only one atom at a time.

The atom remains unavailable to the engine until the item expends it. A creature carrying or wearing the item can use its Infused property. Any saving throw required by the item uses your artificer spell save DC, and any reference to a Transmutation Die uses the die provided by your current metal.

When an item expends an Air, Earth, Fire, or Water atom within 60 feet of you, that atom returns to your engine as Salt. If the item is further away, the atom remains unavailable until you finish a long rest.
When you finish a long rest, every atom still loaded into an infused item dissipates before your engine replenishes its Salt. The items remain infused but must be loaded again.

subclassFeature.name: Metallic Projection
entries: You install a metallic core within your Transmutation Engine. The core begins as Lead and advances through the sequence shown below. The current metal determines your Transmutation Die.

Whenever an Air, Earth, Fire, or Water atom returns to Salt after producing a Bonding effect, the Quicksilver released during the transmutation advances your metallic core to the next metal after the effect is resolved. If the core was Gold, it returns to Lead instead.
The distance of your Air Bond also increases with the current metal, as shown in the Metallic Projection track.

subclassFeature.name: Advanced Alchemical Research
entries: Your research progresses beyond the standard operation of a Transmutation Engine. Choose Classical Alchemy or Experimental Metallurgy. Your choice grants you features now and again at 15th level. Once made, this choice can’t be changed.

entries.name: Classical Alchemy
entries: You pursue the accepted study of vital principles, adding the Glyph of Purification and Glyph of Animismus to your engine.

entries.name: Glyph of Purification
entries: Immediately before you resolve a Bonding effect, you can expend one Salt atom to advance your metallic core by one stage. You resolve the effect using the new metal.
If the bonded atom is Air, Earth, Fire, or Water, the metallic core advances normally after the effect is resolved. You can’t use this glyph while your metallic core is Gold.

entries.name: Glyph of Animismus
entries: As an action, you can transform two Salt atoms within your engine into one Vitae atom and one Mors atom. Your engine can contain only one of each at a time. Vitae and Mors can be used with your Glyph of Bonding.

items.name: Vitae 🜍.
items.entry: The target regains hit points equal to two rolls of your Transmutation Die plus your Intelligence modifier and can end the {@condition poisoned} condition on itself. The Vitae atom is then expended.

items.name: Mors 🜞.
items.entry: The target must make a Constitution saving throw. It takes necrotic damage equal to two rolls of your Transmutation Die on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. On a failed save, it also can’t regain hit points until the start of your next turn. The Mors atom is then expended.

entries.name: Simultaneous Effects
entries: A creature affected by two ongoing instances of the same Bonding effect gains the effect only once. Instantaneous damage, healing, and movement are resolved separately.

entries.name: Experimental Metallurgy
entries: You turn away from the accepted curriculum and subject the metallic sequence to less stable methods, adding the Glyph of Rejection and Glyph of Division to your engine.

entries.name: Glyph of Rejection
entries: When an Air, Earth, Fire, or Water atom produces its Bonding effect while your metallic core is Tin or higher, you can reject the resulting material instead of projecting it. The atom becomes a Quicksilver atom instead of returning to Salt, and your metallic core moves one stage toward Lead instead of advancing toward Gold.
Your engine can contain only one Quicksilver atom at a time. You can’t use Rejection while your metallic core is Lead or while your engine already contains a Quicksilver atom.
Quicksilver can be used with your Glyph of Bonding.

entries.name: Quicksilver ☿
entries: The target can use its reaction to make one weapon attack, cast a cantrip with a casting time of 1 action, or take the Use an Object action. The Quicksilver atom is then expended.

entries.name: Glyph of Division
entries: When you use your Glyph of Bonding with an Air, Earth, Fire, or Water atom while your metallic core is Tin or higher, you can divide the metal and resolve the Bonding effect twice. The effects can have the same target or different eligible targets.

For each effect, use the metal shown in the Divided Metals table instead of your current metal. After both effects are resolved, your metallic core returns to Lead. The atom is processed only once, and no additional atom or Salt is created.
Once you use this glyph, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Completed Research
entries: Your chosen course of research reaches its final form. You gain the feature associated with the research path you chose at 9th level.

entries.name: Quintessential Cycle
entries: Your Glyph of Purification no longer expends a Salt atom when you use it. You can still use the glyph only once for each Bonding effect.
You also add the Glyph of Unification and Glyph of Dispersion to your engine.

entries.name: Cardinal Inputs
entries: When you finish a short or long rest, you can replace four Salt atoms within your engine with one Air, Earth, Fire, and Water atom.

entries.name: Glyph of Unification
entries: As a bonus action, you can transform one Air, Earth, Fire, and Water atom within your engine into one Quintessence atom. Your engine can contain only one Quintessence atom at a time.
Once you create a Quintessence atom, you can’t create another until you finish a short or long rest.

entries.name: Glyph of Dispersion
entries: As a bonus action, you can separate one Quintessence atom within your engine into one Air, Earth, Fire, and Water atom.
Quintessence can also be used with your Glyph of Bonding.

entries.name: Quintessence
entries: Choose a willing creature as the target. It assumes a perfected form for 1 minute and gains the following benefits:

items: It has resistance to all damage.
It gains a flying speed equal to twice its walking speed and can hover.
It can move through creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. If it ends its turn inside an object, it takes {@damage 2d8} force damage and is moved to the nearest unoccupied space.

It can’t be {@condition charmed}, {@condition frightened}, {@condition paralyzed}, {@condition petrified}, {@condition poisoned}, or {@condition restrained}, and each of those conditions affecting it ends when the Bond begins.
Once during each of its turns when it deals damage or restores hit points, it can deal or restore additional hit points equal to one roll of your Transmutation Die.

entries: The effect ends early if the creature is {@condition incapacitated}. When the effect ends, the Quintessence separates into four Salt atoms, which return to your engine. Once you bond Quintessence in this way, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Glyph of Proliferation
entries: When your engine contains a Quicksilver atom, you can use a bonus action to feed it into your current metallic core, creating a second identical core. The Quicksilver atom is expended, and both cores remain at the metal your core contained when you activated this glyph for the duration. As part of the same bonus action, you can use your Glyph of Bonding.
For 1 minute, your engine gains the following benefits:

items: At the start of each of your turns, you can convert one Salt atom within your engine into an Air, Earth, Fire, or Water atom of your choice.

Once during each of your turns when you produce a Bonding effect, the second core reproduces that effect. Resolve the effect a second time using the metal duplicated by this glyph, choosing the same target or another eligible target.

entries: Only the effect is produced twice. The bonded atom is processed once and returns to Salt or is expended normally. Proliferation never creates additional atoms or Salt.

You can’t use your Glyph of Rejection or Glyph of Division while Proliferation is active. When this effect ends, the duplicated core destabilizes and disappears as it turns into Salt while your original core remains at the metal duplicated by this glyph. When this effects ends, you restore Salt atoms up to the number that have been expended, not counting those placed on Infusions.
Once you activate this glyph, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

entries.name: Conservation of Matter
entries: Proliferation repeats the result of a Bonding effect. It doesn’t create or process a second atom, and it can’t return more Salt than the original Bonding effect would have returned.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Broodmother
entries: Druids of the Circle of the Broodmother venerate Oraxia, the Lady of Webs. An ancient guardian abandoned within a realm that vanished from the world. There, a presence from beyond creation whispered in the voice of her absent master, twisting her devotion into madness and transforming her into the embodiment of sinister grace, and predatory perfection.

Her followers preserve the Lady’s fragmented traditions and teachings, seeking to mirror her evolution without sharing her fate. They awaken arachnid limbs, cultivate supernatural toxins, and nurture broods within the bodies of fallen prey. To them, the perfect predator does not kill through savagery alone, but through patience, and mercy of a swift final strike.

entries.name: Silken Stride
entries: When you choose this circle at 2nd level, you can use your Wild Shape to awaken the arachnid form inspired by the greatness of the Lady of Webs.

As a bonus action, you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to channel the teachings of the Lady of Webs, rather than transforming into a beast form, and you gain 4 temporary hit points for each level you have in this class.
While this feature is active, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed, and you can move up, down, and across vertical surfaces and upside down along ceilings while leaving your hands free.

You manifest spider limbs that are natural weapons, which you can use to make unarmed strikes. When you attack with them, you can use your Wisdom modifier, instead of Strength, for the attack and damage rolls. On a hit, they deal piercing damage equal to {@damage 1d6} + your Wisdom modifier.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack or an unarmed strike, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} poison or necrotic damage to it. You choose the damage type each time you deal this additional damage.

entries: These benefits last for 10 minutes, until you lose all these temporary hit points, or until you use your Wild Shape again.

entries.name: Brood Forms
entries: The Lady of Webs is considered to be the pinnacle of nature by her followers, who mirror her greatness by taking the shapes of creatures that reflect her many children.
When you use Wild Shape, you can transform into a creature from the Brood Forms table, provided you have reached the required druid level.

entries.caption: Brood Forms
rows: {@creature Giant Wolf Spider|MM}, {@creature Swarm of Insects|MM} (as spiders)
{@creature Phase Spider|MM}, {@creature Giant Scorpion|MM} (as a spider)

entries: You can assume the form even if its creature type, challenge rating, or movement speeds would normally prevent you from doing so. Except for these allowances, the normal rules of Wild Shape apply.

entries.name: Circle Spells
entries: Your connection to the Lady of Webs grants you access to certain spells. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level, you gain access to the spells listed for that level in the Circle of the Broodmother Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn’t count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn’t appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

entries.name: Toxin
entries: Also at 2nd level, your attacks and magic infect creatures with supernatural toxins.

Whenever one or more creatures take poison or necrotic damage from you, you can give one {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counter to each of those creatures. A creature can have a maximum number of your {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters equal to your proficiency bonus.

A creature’s speed is reduced by 5 feet for each of your {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters it has. While a creature has a number of your {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters equal to your proficiency bonus, it is also {@condition poisoned}.

At the end of each of its turns, a creature with one or more of your {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters can make a Constitution saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a successful save, it removes one {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counter. All your {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters on a creature disappear if it has not gained one of your {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters for 1 minute.

{@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} is a magical effect. A creature immune to the {@condition poisoned} condition can still accumulate {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters and suffer their reduction to its speed, but it can’t become poisoned by this feature.

subclassFeature.name: Widow's Brood
entries: Starting at 6th level, the dead provide nourishment from which your spiderlings emerge.

When a Small or larger hostile creature with one or more of your {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters dies within 60 feet of you, you can use your reaction and expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher to produce a number of Spiderlings equal to the level of the expended spell slot. The Spiderlings emerge in the dead creature’s space or the nearest unoccupied space and collectively form a {@creature Spiderling Brood|TwofellCircleBroodmother}.

The Brood can contain a maximum number of Spiderlings equal to your proficiency bonus. If you already have a Spiderling Brood, the new Spiderlings join it rather than creating another Brood. The Brood disappears after 1 hour, when its last Spiderling dies, or when you die. Adding Spiderlings to the Brood restarts this duration.
The Brood is friendly to you and your companions and obeys your telepathic commands.

In combat, the Brood shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It obeys your telepathic commands, which require no action from you. If you issue it no commands, it takes the Dodge action and uses its movement to avoid danger. If you are {@condition incapacitated}, the Brood acts independently, focusing on protecting you and itself.

Additionally, attacks made by the Brood and attacks made using the natural weapons of your Brood Forms count as magical for the purpose of overcoming resistance and immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage.

subclassFeature.name: Virulent Brood
entries: At 10th level, the {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} running through your Brood becomes capable of spreading and binding prey within living webs. You gain the following benefits:

items: The additional poison or necrotic damage dealt by your Silken Stride increases to {@damage 2d6}.
Poison and necrotic damage dealt by your Silken Stride, your Brood Forms, and your Spiderling Brood ignores resistance to those damage types.
When your Spiderling Brood deals poison damage to a creature, you can give that creature one of your {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters.
You can cast {@spell web|phb} once without expending a spell slot or material components. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a long rest.

When you cast {@spell web|phb}, you can remove any number of your {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters from each creature in the spell’s area. A creature from which you remove at least one {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counter has disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against that casting of the spell. If it fails that saving throw, it takes {@damage 1d10} poison damage for each {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counter removed from it.

subclassFeature.name: Mercy's Kiss
entries: At 14th level, you can sense when infected prey stands at the boundary between life and death. While your Silken Stride is active or you are in a Brood Form, you know when a creature you can see within 60 feet of you has one or more of your {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters and has hit points equal to or less than 20 percent of its hit point maximum, rounded down.
As an action, you can choose one such creature within 60 feet of you and leap to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it. This movement doesn’t expend your movement or provoke opportunity attacks.

You pierce the creature with your spider limbs and remove all your {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counters from it. If the creature doesn’t have the Legendary Resistance trait, legendary actions, or lair actions, it dies. Otherwise, it takes {@damage 1d10} piercing damage and {@damage 1d10} poison damage for each {@condition Toxin|TwofellCircleBroodmother} counter removed.

There are many ways for a Wizard to hone their intellect and better control the Weave. Some discover new spells, while others refine what already exists and share that knowledge with anyone willing to learn.
Professors belong firmly to that last group.
To them, magic is something to be tested, taught and corrected. The insights of others can reveal possibilities the Professor may never have considered alone.

Eventually, a simple spell becomes something distinctly theirs; covered in amendments and notes on what to do and not to do. Magic refined through experience and carrying the work of everyone who helped shape it.

subclassFeature.name: Thesis
entries: Beginning when you choose this tradition at 2nd level, choose one 1st-level wizard spell in your spellbook to be your {@filter Thesis Spell|spells|level=1|class=wizard|components & miscellaneous=!ritual;!reprinted|cast time=action}. The chosen spell must meet all of the following requirements:

items: It has a casting time of 1 action.
It doesn't have the ritual tag.
It doesn't consume its material components.
It doesn't summon or create a creature, and it doesn't create an object that remains after the spell ends.

entries: Your Thesis Spell is always prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of wizard spells you can prepare.

Whenever you gain a level in this class before reaching 14th level, you can replace your Thesis Spell with another eligible spell in your spellbook. When you do so, you can also replace any number of Revisions you know with other Revisions for which you meet the prerequisites.

entries.name: Insight
entries: You gain Insight as described in your Shared Thesis feature.
You can have a maximum number of Insight points equal to your proficiency bonus. You lose all unspent Insight when you finish a long rest.

entries.name: 2nd-Level Revisions
entries: You learn three Revisions of your choice from the Thesis Revisions presented at the end of this subclass. You learn two additional Revisions when you reach 6th, 10th, and 14th level in this class.
Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one Revision you know with another Revision for which you meet the prerequisites.

When you cast your Thesis Spell, you can spend Insight to apply one or more Revisions you know to that casting. Unless a Revision states otherwise, it costs 1 Insight to apply. The maximum number of Revisions you can apply to a single casting is shown in the Professor Features table.
You can't apply the same Revision more than once to the same casting.

subclassFeature.name: Shared Thesis
entries: When you finish a long rest, you can create a number of physical magical copies of your Thesis Spell equal to your proficiency bonus. You can distribute these copies among willing allies that finished the rest within 30 feet of you, can understand at least one language you speak, and weren't summoned or created by a spell or class feature. An ally can receive more than one copy.

An ally can use its action to expend one of its copies and cast your Thesis Spell at its lowest level without expending a spell slot. The ally uses your spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus for the spell. The ally must maintain concentration on the spell if it requires concentration, using the copy as an arcane focus for the casting.

A copy can be used only by the ally to which you gave it to, representing the task of addapting the casting to that specific creature's understanding. Any unused copies lose their magic when you finish your next long rest.

You can also use your action and expend a spell slot of a level equal to or greater than your Thesis Spell's level to create one additional copy of the spell and give it to a willing ally within your reach.
When an ally within 60 feet of you casts your Thesis Spell using one of your copies and you can see or hear that ally, you gain 1 Insight after the spell is cast.

subclassFeature.name: Established Method
entries: Starting at 6th level, choose one Revision you know that costs 1 Insight. That Revision becomes your Established Method.

Whenever an ally casts your Thesis Spell using one of your copies, your Established Method can be applied to that casting without spending Insight. It counts against the maximum number of Revisions you can apply to the casting.
Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace your Established Method with another Revision you know that meets the requirements above.

subclassFeature.name: Peer Review
entries: Starting at 10th level, when an ally you can see within 60 feet of you casts your Thesis Spell using one of your copies, you can use your reaction to apply one additional Revision you know to that casting. You must spend the normal amount of Insight for the Revision, and the Revision must be able to apply to that casting.
This Revision is applied in addition to your Established Method.

subclassFeature.name: Advanced Thesis
entries: Starting at 10th level, your {@filter Thesis Spell|spells|level=1;2|class=wizard|components & miscellaneous=!ritual;!reprinted|cast time=action} can be a 1st- or 2nd-level wizard spell in your spellbook that meets the requirements of your Thesis feature.

subclassFeature.name: Magnum Opus
entries: Starting at 14th level, your Thesis Spell becomes your Magnum Opus and can no longer be replaced.
Choose a second Revision you know that costs 1 Insight. This Revision also becomes part of your Established Method.
Whenever an ally casts your Magnum Opus using one of your copies, both Revisions that make up your Established Method can be applied to that casting without spending Insight.

Whenever you cast your Magnum Opus, both Revisions that make up your Established Method are applied to that casting without spending Insight. They count against the maximum number of Revisions you can apply to the casting.

In addition, you can cast your Magnum Opus once as a 5th-level spell without spending a spell slot. When you do so, you can apply up to four Revisions you know to the casting without spending Insight. Once you cast the spell in this way, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Street Magic
entries: Street Magicians are performers that take the usual tricks and sleights of hand a little further than most expect. They still carry the usual: cards, coins, flowers and cheap wands, but somewhere along the way learned how to hide genuine magic among those tricks. Meant to both enhance and deceive their opponents as previously harmless tricks can prove to be fatal in their sleeves.

There are plenty of ways to play a Street Magician. You can be a performer that slowly pushed their tricks further, someone that stole a few routines from a mentor, or a failed magical student that realized fireballs get a better reaction when they come out of a deck of cards. Whatever the case, magic is simply another part of their performance and they love the show.
When you reach 3rd level, you gain the ability to cast spells through a collection of practiced Tricks.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You learn the {@spell prestidigitation|phb} cantrip and two other cantrips of your choice from the wizard spell list. The latter two cantrips must be Evocation spells with a casting time of 1 action. You learn another wizard cantrip that meets these requirements at 10th level.
These cantrips and the spells you learn as Tricks are Street Magician spells for you.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Street Magician spells, since you work your magic through practiced performances and convincing presentation. You use your Charisma whenever a spell refers to your spellcasting ability. In addition, you use your Charisma modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a Street Magician spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.

entries.name: Trick Skill
entries: Choose either {@skill Performance} or {@skill Sleight of Hand}. You gain proficiency in the chosen skill if you don’t already have it.
Whenever one of your Street Magician features calls for a Trick Check, you make the check using the skill chosen for this feature.

entries.name: Enhanced Prestidigitation
entries: When you cast {@spell prestidigitation|phb}, you can create one of the following magical effects instead of one of the spell’s normal effects:

items: You cause a playing card, coin, flower, handkerchief, or similarly sized object you are holding to vanish and immediately reappear in another empty hand.

You cause a playing card, piece of paper, or flammable Tiny object you are holding to harmlessly catch fire until the end of your next turn. The fire doesn’t damage the object, but it can ignite other flammable objects that aren’t being worn or carried.
You spray a stream of water from a prop you are holding toward a point you can see within 10 feet of you.

entries.name: Tricks Known of 1st Level and Higher
entries: You know three 1st-level wizard spells of your choice. Each spell must be an Evocation spell with a casting time of 1 action. These spells are your Tricks.

The Tricks Known column of the Street Magician Tricks table shows when you learn more Tricks. Each of these spells must be an Evocation spell from the wizard spell list, must have a casting time of 1 action, and can be no higher in level than the Maximum Trick Level shown for your rogue level.

See {@link spells able to be picked for Trick Spells|https://2014.5e.tools/spells.html#affirm%20gender_lewdhandbook,flstsource:aag=1~ai=1~bmt=1~egw=1~ftd=1~ggr=1~phb=1~sato=1~tce=1~xge=1~rmr=1~qftis=1~tofw=1~veor=1~mot=1~scag=1~eepc=1~erlw=1~vgm=1~lewdhandbook=1,flstlevel:0=1~1=1~2=1~3=1~4=1~5=1,flstclass:wizard=1,flstcomponents%20%26%20miscellaneous:,flstschool:v=1,flstcast%20time:action=1}.

Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace one Trick you know with another spell of your choice from the wizard spell list. The new spell must be an Evocation spell, must have a casting time of 1 action, and can be no higher in level than your Maximum Trick Level.

entries.name: Trick Points
entries: You have a number of Trick Points equal to your proficiency bonus. You can’t have more Trick Points than your proficiency bonus.

entries.name: Performing a Trick
entries: You can cast one of your Tricks without expending a spell slot. To do so, you must spend a number of Trick Points equal to the spell’s level.

When you perform a Trick, a number of your Sneak Attack dice equal to the spell’s level become unavailable until the start of your next turn. An unavailable Sneak Attack die can’t be rolled as part of your Sneak Attack or made unavailable to perform another Trick.
You can’t perform a Trick unless you have enough Trick Points and available Sneak Attack dice to do so.

If a Trick has an increased effect when cast at a higher level, you can cast it at a higher level, up to your Maximum Trick Level. The number of Trick Points you spend and Sneak Attack dice that become unavailable are determined by the level at which you cast the spell.

entries.name: Trick Check
entries: Whenever you perform a Trick, make an ability check using the skill chosen for your Trick Skill. The DC equals 10 + twice the level at which you cast the spell.

The spell is cast regardless of the result of the check. If you fail the check, something in the routine goes wrong after the spell takes effect. The Trick becomes Spoiled, and you can’t perform that Trick again until you use your action to reset it.
If the result of the check exceeds the DC by 5 or more, you regain 1 expended Trick Point after the spell is cast.

entries.name: Quick Flourish
entries: On your turn, if you haven’t performed a Trick, you can use a bonus action to cast {@spell prestidigitation|phb} and perform a brief flourish, provided you can see a hostile creature within 60 feet of you.
When you do so, make a Trick Check against DC 15. On a successful check, you regain 1 expended Trick Point.

entries.name: Rehearse the Act
entries: You regain all expended Trick Points when you finish a short or long rest. You can also regain all expended Trick Points by spending 1 minute rehearsing your routines, provided there are no hostile creatures that you can see or hear within 60 feet of you.
When you rehearse your act in this way, you also reset all of your Spoiled Tricks.

entries.name: Tools of the Trade
entries: You can use a playing card set or an arcane focus as a spellcasting focus for your Street Magician spells.

subclassFeature.name: Magician's Strike
entries: You learn to exploit the opening created by a well-timed magical performance. When you hit a creature with a spell attack made as part of one of your Tricks or Street Magician cantrips, you can deal your Sneak Attack damage with that attack if you have advantage on the attack roll.
You don’t need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn’t {@condition incapacitated}, and you don’t have disadvantage on the attack roll.
You can deal Sneak Attack damage in this way only once per turn, and you can roll only your currently available Sneak Attack dice.

subclassFeature.name: Something Up Your Sleeve
entries: You keep a collection of unfinished routines for those moments when whatever is left in your sleeve is better than nothing.

Whenever you finish a long rest, choose six different Evocation spells from the wizard spell list and assign each one a number from 1 to 6. Each spell must have a casting time of 1 action and be of a level no higher than your Maximum Trick Level. These spells form your Emergency Hand until you finish your next long rest. They are Street Magician spells for you and don’t count against your number of Tricks Known.

As an action, roll a {@dice d6}. You then cast the spell corresponding to the number rolled as a Trick. You don’t expend Trick Points to perform this Trick, but you must still have enough available Sneak Attack dice to perform it and make its Trick Check as normal.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Practiced Hand
entries: Your routines have become second nature, allowing you to work more complicated magic without compromising the rest of your performance.
When you perform a Trick of 2nd level or higher, one fewer Sneak Attack die becomes unavailable, to a minimum of one die.
In addition, when you use your Something Up Your Sleeve feature, roll the d6 twice and choose which of the two results to use.
When the result of a Trick Check exceeds its DC by 5 or more, you can reset one Spoiled Trick instead of regaining 1 expended Trick Point.

subclassFeature.name: Grand Trick
entries: You perfect a single routine beyond everything else in your repertoire.

Choose one Evocation spell of 5th level or lower from the wizard spell list. The spell must have a casting time of 1 action. The chosen spell is a Street Magician spell for you, becomes your Grand Trick, and doesn’t count against your number of Tricks Known.

You can perform your Grand Trick as a 5th-level Trick, even though it exceeds your Maximum Trick Level. When you do so, you spend 5 Trick Points and otherwise follow the rules for Performing a Trick and making its Trick Check.
Once you perform your Grand Trick in this way, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.
If your Grand Trick is also one of your Tricks, you can still perform it normally at any level allowed by your Maximum Trick Level.
Whenever you gain a level in this class, you can replace your Grand Trick with another spell that meets these requirements.

entries.name: Hype
entries: Hype is a special kind of temporary hit points granted by your Idol Agency features, pact songs, or spells given or modified by this subclass.
When a creature that already has hype from you gains hype from you, the new hype is added to the old hype, instead of replacing it.

entries.name: Fan
entries: A creature with hype from you is one of your fans. When a creature has no hype from you, it stops being your fan.
A creature’s maximum hype from you equals twice your warlock level + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus (min. 1).

entries.name: Separate Sources
entries: Each creature that grants hype tracks that hype separately. A creature can’t have hype from, or be a fan of, more than one creature at a time. When it gains hype from a new source, it chooses whether to keep its current hype or replace it with the new hype, using the new source’s maximum, duration, and associated effects.

entries.name: Hype Rules Reference
entries: Hype functions as temporary hit points except where these rules state otherwise.
Hype doesn’t stack with temporary hit points from sources other than you.
When a creature with hype from you gains temporary hit points from another source, it chooses whether to keep its hype or gain those temporary hit points, as normal.
If hype from a spell or feature has a duration, that hype disappears when its duration ends.
Unless the effect granting hype states otherwise, the hype disappears when the creature finishes a long rest.

entries.name: Public Image Department
entries: The rules use the words hype and fan, but the character does not need to be famous or possess significant social standing. Hype can represent morale, euphoria, courage, devotion, or another emotion the performer inspires. Use whatever presentation best fits your version of the story.

subclassFeature.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Idol Agency lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you.

subclassFeature.name: Agency Training
entries: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance} skill. If you already have this proficiency, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses Performance.
You also learn the {@spell guidance} cantrip. It counts as a warlock cantrip for you, but it doesn’t count against your number of cantrips known.

You can use a musical instrument or any object associated with your performances, such as a microphone, fan, mask, glowstick or performance costume, as a spellcasting focus for your warlock spells. The object must be worth at least 1 gp, and you must hold or wear it to use it in this way.

subclassFeature.name: Cheer Up!
entries: You learn the {@spell false life} spell. It counts as a warlock spell for you, but it doesn’t count against your number of warlock spells known.
When you cast {@spell false life}, you can cast it as though it had a range of 30 feet, targeting a willing creature within range instead of yourself.
When you cast {@spell false life} using a warlock spell slot, you can target a number of willing creatures within 30 feet of you equal to your proficiency bonus. Roll separately for each target.
Temporary hit points granted by {@spell false life} in this way are hype.

entries.name: Only false life cast by expending a spell slot can grant Hype.
entries: {@spell false life} cast without expending a spell slot, such as through the {@optfeature Fiendish Vigor} invocation, does not grant hype.

subclassFeature.name: We Rehearsed This!
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you is hit by an attack or fails a saving throw, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to its AC against the triggering attack or to its saving throw, potentially causing the attack to miss or the saving throw to succeed.
If the creature is one of your fans, it can also move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Uncancellable
entries: You gain resistance to psychic damage and you have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed}.
Your fans also gain these benefits while they have hype from you.
In addition, when you cast {@spell guidance} on one of your fans, the die rolled for the spell becomes a {@dice d6} instead of a {@dice d4}.

When one of your fans would lose all of its hype as a result of taking damage, it retains 1 hype instead. Once a creature benefits from this feature, it can’t do so again until it finishes a short or long rest.

subclassFeature.name: One Last Song!
entries: You can begin an encore. As an action, you can choose up to six creatures within 60 feet of you, including yourself. Each chosen creature gains hype equal to twice your warlock level + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus.
Hype granted by this feature lasts for 1 minute.
For the duration, your fans who have hype from this feature gain the following benefits:

items: Their speed increases by 10 feet.
Their movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.
Once per turn, before making an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, a fan can spend 5 hype to roll {@dice 1d6} and add the number rolled to the result.

entries: Encore ends early if you are {@condition incapacitated} or die.
Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Master of the Unseen Hand
entries: Masters of the Unseen Hand refine their studies into two related forms of magic. Using a simple spell like  {@i mage hands} to their absolute limit as they multiply into a collection of dexterous assistants capable of carrying out several delicate tasks at once, while their greater telekinetic power seizes creatures and heavy objects with overwhelming invisible force.

For a wizard, this discipline is an Arcane Tradition built upon keeping concentration while multitasking control upon multiple hands. For a bard, it is a Bard College whose force of will helps them conduct these hands as though directing an invisible ensemble.

entries.name: Master of the Unseen Hand Features
entries: When you select this subclass, it becomes your subclass for that class. You can't select Master of the Unseen Hand as the subclass for another class.

entries.name: Unseen Hand Level
entries: Some features of this subclass refer to your {@b Unseen Hand level}. Your Unseen Hand level equals your combined levels in the bard and wizard classes. For example, if you are a 4th-level bard and a 6th-level wizard, your Unseen Hand level is 10.

Your Unseen Hand level determines the strength of features you already possess; it doesn't grant subclass features earlier than you're supposed to gain them. You gain each feature based on your level in the class through which you selected this subclass.

subclassFeature.name: Many Hands
entries: You learn the {@spell mage hand|PHB} cantrip. It is a spell of the class through which you gained this subclass, and it doesn't count against the number of cantrips you know. If you already know {@spell mage hand|PHB} from that class, you learn another cantrip of your choice from that class's spell list.

When you cast {@spell mage hand|PHB}, you can create multiple spectral hands instead of creating one. The number of hands you create is shown in the Many Hands table. You choose the appearance of these hands each time you cast the spell.

The hands share the spell's duration and range. Each hand can move independently, can carry no more than 10 pounds, and vanishes if it ends its turn more than 30 feet from you. A hand also vanishes if you dismiss it (no action required). The spell ends when its last hand vanishes.

When you use your action to control the hands, you can move each of them up to 30 feet and command each hand to perform one task permitted by {@spell mage hand|PHB}. If a task would require an ability check, only one hand can attempt one per round. They can work together to lift one object that exceeds an individual hand's carrying capacity, so long as its weight doesn't exceed their combined carrying capacity.
You can also control only one of the hands as a bonus action, moving it and commanding it to perform one task permitted by the spell.

subclassFeature.name: Skilled Handiwork
entries: Hands summoned by the mage hand cantrip can apply the skills you have practiced. Each hand can hold and use a tool or musical instrument with which you are proficient. Your hands can perform simple, practiced tasks such as holding books open, turning its pages, writing dictated words, playing instruments, stirring a mixture, or organizing your equipment.

When you use your action to control the hands, you can command one hand to perform a task that requires an ability check using a tool, an instrument, or a skill in which you are proficient. You make the check as though you were performing the task yourself, provided you can see both the hand and the subject of its work. The task must be physically possible using only the hand and the objects within its reach.

A hand can hold your spellcasting focus, or a material component, but this doesn't allow you to provide a spell's components remotely, cast a spell from the hand's space, or ignore any components of a spell.

entries.name: Many Hands, One Will
entries: The hands can look and behave independently. A scholar might surround herself with spectral scribes, while a bard conducts them as a silent ensemble of instruments and props.

subclassFeature.name: Practiced Hands
entries: Your spectral hands coordinate with practiced efficiency. When two or more hands work together on a task permitted by your Skilled Handiwork, you have advantage on one ability check made for that task, provided it could reasonably benefit from the additional hands.

In addition, when you use your bonus action to control one hand, that hand can perform a task permitted by your Skilled Handiwork that requires an ability check. Once a hand makes an ability check on your turn, none of your other hands can make another ability check until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Forceful Hands
entries: Your spectral hands can exert enough force to fight. When you use your action to control the hands created by your {@spell mage hand|PHB}, you can make the attacks described under Telekinetic Wielder.
You can replace any of those attacks with one Unseen Grasp maneuver.

entries.name: Telekinetic Wielder
entries: As part of the action you use to control your hands, each hand you command to attack can pick up one nonmagical melee weapon within 5 feet of it. The weapon can't have the two-handed property and must weigh no more than the hand's carrying capacity. A hand can carry only one weapon at a time.

You can then command one hand carrying a weapon to attack a creature within 5 feet of that hand. Make a melee spell attack using the spellcasting ability of the class through which you gained this subclass. On a hit, the target takes damage equal to one roll of the weapon's damage die plus your spellcasting ability modifier. The damage is of a type dealt by the weapon. A versatile weapon uses its one-handed damage die for this attack.

You can make two attacks in this way when your Unseen Hand level reaches 10. Each attack must be made by a different hand wielding a different weapon, and the attacks can target the same creature or different ones.

When your Unseen Hand level reaches 10, your hands can wield magic weapons. You must be attuned to such a weapon if it requires attunement. The hand's attack benefits from the weapon's bonus to attack and damage rolls and from any of its properties that trigger when an attack made with it hits. A hand can't activate a magic weapon, and neither you nor the hand gains any other property that requires the weapon to be held or wielded.

entries.name: Unseen Grasp
entries: When you replace an attack with this option, choose one empty hand and one Medium or smaller creature within 5 feet of it. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or suffer one of the following effects of your choice:

items: {@b Disarm.} The target releases one object of your choice that it is holding. If the object weighs no more than the hand's carrying capacity, the hand catches it.
{@b Drive.} The hand moves the target up to 10 feet toward or away from itself.
{@b Topple.} The target falls prone.

entries: When your Unseen Hand level reaches 10, these maneuvers can affect a Large or smaller creature. A creature can be targeted by only one Unseen Grasp maneuver during the same action.
A hand must release anything it is carrying before it can attempt an Unseen Grasp maneuver.

entries.name: Weapons Without Wielders
entries: A Master's weapons do not spring from nothing. Each blade must be present on the battlefield or carried by their user before the hands can seize it and turn it against an enemy.

subclassFeature.name: Sustained Force
entries: You learn the {@spell telekinesis|PHB} spell. It counts as a spell of the class through which you gained this subclass

If you are a wizard, the spell is added to your spellbook and is always prepared for you. If {@spell telekinesis|PHB} is already in your spellbook, you can add one other wizard spell of 5th level or lower to your spellbook instead.

If you are a bard, {@spell telekinesis|PHB} doesn't count against the number of bard spells you know. If you already know {@spell telekinesis|PHB} as a bard spell, you can immediately replace that spell with another bard spell for which you have spell slots; the replacement spell counts against the number of bard spells you know as normal.
You can cast {@spell telekinesis|PHB} once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a long rest.
While you concentrate on {@spell telekinesis|PHB}, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain concentration on the spell.

After the turn on which you cast the spell, you can use a bonus action, rather than an action, to exert your will over the spell's target or to choose a new target. Provided you don't cast another spell using your action on that turn.

You can cast and control {@spell mage hand|PHB} normally. Controlling your {@spell mage hand|PHB} with your action doesn't prevent you from using {@spell telekinesis|PHB} with your bonus action on the same turn.

When you target yourself or a willing creature with the creature option of {@spell telekinesis|PHB}, no ability check is required, and the target isn't restrained. Whenever you exert your will over that target, you can move it up to 30 feet in any direction, but not beyond the spell's range. The target remains suspended between these movements.

subclassFeature.name: Versatile Telekinesis
entries: Your {@spell telekinesis|PHB} can build from careful control into sudden, overwhelming force, granting you the following options. Once you use one of these options, you can't use that option again until the next time you cast {@spell telekinesis|PHB}.

entries.name: Violent Thrust
entries: As an action, choose one Large or smaller creature or one unattended object that you can see within the spell's range. When your Unseen Hand level reaches 17, you can choose up to two creatures or objects, and a chosen creature can be Huge or smaller. A chosen object can weigh no more than 1,000 pounds.

Each chosen creature must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes {@dice 4d10} bludgeoning damage, is hurled up to 30 feet in a direction you choose, and falls prone. It must end this movement in an unoccupied space, and it can't end more than 10 feet higher than where it began. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't moved.

You can hurl each chosen object up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Alternatively, you can hurl the object at a creature within 30 feet of it. Make a ranged spell attack against the creature. On a hit, the target takes {@dice 4d10} bludgeoning damage, and the object falls into an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it. On a miss, the object falls into an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target.

If a hurled creature would enter another creature's space during this movement, the other creature must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the other creature takes {@dice 4d10} bludgeoning damage, and the hurled creature's movement ends in the nearest unoccupied space before the collision. On a successful save, the other creature takes no damage, and the hurled creature continues moving. The hurled creature takes no additional damage from the collision.
Using Violent Thrust releases any target currently held by telekinesis.

entries.name: Fling Skyward
entries: As an action, choose one Large or smaller creature currently restrained by your telekinesis. When your Unseen Hand level reaches 17, you can choose a Huge or smaller creature. The target must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you swing the target in a rising arc and fling it 120 feet straight upward. It remains suspended and restrained there until the start of your next turn, when it falls. On a successful save, the target isn't flung and remains restrained by telekinesis.

If the target strikes a solid surface before completing this movement, its upward movement ends. It takes {@dice 1d6} bludgeoning damage for every 15 feet of the 120-foot movement prevented by the collision, and then immediately falls.
On a failed save, the target is released from {@spell telekinesis|PHB} after being flung.

{@b Drive.} The hand moves the target up to 10 feet toward or away from itself.
