entries: When your Unseen Hand level reaches 10, these maneuvers can affect a Large or smaller creature. A creature can be targeted by only one Unseen Grasp maneuver during the same action.
A hand must release anything it is carrying before it can attempt an Unseen Grasp maneuver.

entries.name: Weapons Without Wielders
entries: A Master's weapons do not spring from nothing. Each blade must be present on the battlefield or carried by their user before the hands can seize it and turn it against an enemy.

subclassFeature.name: Sustained Force
entries: You learn the {@spell telekinesis|PHB} spell. It counts as a spell of the class through which you gained this subclass

If you are a wizard, the spell is added to your spellbook and is always prepared for you. If {@spell telekinesis|PHB} is already in your spellbook, you can add one other wizard spell of 5th level or lower to your spellbook instead.

If you are a bard, {@spell telekinesis|PHB} doesn't count against the number of bard spells you know. If you already know {@spell telekinesis|PHB} as a bard spell, you can immediately replace that spell with another bard spell for which you have spell slots; the replacement spell counts against the number of bard spells you know as normal.
You can cast {@spell telekinesis|PHB} once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast it in this way when you finish a long rest.
While you concentrate on {@spell telekinesis|PHB}, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain concentration on the spell.

After the turn on which you cast the spell, you can use a bonus action, rather than an action, to exert your will over the spell's target or to choose a new target. Provided you don't cast another spell using your action on that turn.

You can cast and control {@spell mage hand|PHB} normally. Controlling your {@spell mage hand|PHB} with your action doesn't prevent you from using {@spell telekinesis|PHB} with your bonus action on the same turn.

When you target yourself or a willing creature with the creature option of {@spell telekinesis|PHB}, no ability check is required, and the target isn't restrained. Whenever you exert your will over that target, you can move it up to 30 feet in any direction, but not beyond the spell's range. The target remains suspended between these movements.

subclassFeature.name: Versatile Telekinesis
entries: Your {@spell telekinesis|PHB} can build from careful control into sudden, overwhelming force, granting you the following options. Once you use one of these options, you can't use that option again until the next time you cast {@spell telekinesis|PHB}.

entries.name: Violent Thrust
entries: As an action, choose one Large or smaller creature or one unattended object that you can see within the spell's range. When your Unseen Hand level reaches 17, you can choose up to two creatures or objects, and a chosen creature can be Huge or smaller. A chosen object can weigh no more than 1,000 pounds.

Each chosen creature must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature takes {@dice 4d10} bludgeoning damage, is hurled up to 30 feet in a direction you choose, and falls prone. It must end this movement in an unoccupied space, and it can't end more than 10 feet higher than where it began. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and isn't moved.

You can hurl each chosen object up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. Alternatively, you can hurl the object at a creature within 30 feet of it. Make a ranged spell attack against the creature. On a hit, the target takes {@dice 4d10} bludgeoning damage, and the object falls into an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it. On a miss, the object falls into an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target.

If a hurled creature would enter another creature's space during this movement, the other creature must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the other creature takes {@dice 4d10} bludgeoning damage, and the hurled creature's movement ends in the nearest unoccupied space before the collision. On a successful save, the other creature takes no damage, and the hurled creature continues moving. The hurled creature takes no additional damage from the collision.
Using Violent Thrust releases any target currently held by telekinesis.

entries.name: Fling Skyward
entries: As an action, choose one Large or smaller creature currently restrained by your telekinesis. When your Unseen Hand level reaches 17, you can choose a Huge or smaller creature. The target must make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you swing the target in a rising arc and fling it 120 feet straight upward. It remains suspended and restrained there until the start of your next turn, when it falls. On a successful save, the target isn't flung and remains restrained by telekinesis.

If the target strikes a solid surface before completing this movement, its upward movement ends. It takes {@dice 1d6} bludgeoning damage for every 15 feet of the 120-foot movement prevented by the collision, and then immediately falls.
On a failed save, the target is released from {@spell telekinesis|PHB} after being flung.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Foxfire
entries: Paladins who swear the Oath of the Foxfire serve as exorcists and mediators between the living and the dead. Each is accompanied by a spirit fox whose flames help reveal what is concealed. Their task is to shelter peaceful spirits, and burn corruption from those it has claimed. As the bond between Paladin and spirit deepens, the fox develops additional tails and reveals more of its kitsune nature.

These Paladins do not assume every lingering spirit is malicious, instead they seek to uncover the truth behind their actions. Hoping to preserve spirits that mean no harm, and cleanse those that can still be saved. Only spirits beyond redemption are consigned to the foxfire.

rows: Oath Spells, Channel Divinity, One-Tailed Fox

entries.name: Tenets of the Foxfire
entries: The tenets of the Oath of the Foxfire teach a Paladin to temper vigilance with compassion.
{@b See Beyond the Veil.} Seek the truth even when it is concealed by magic or deception.
{@b Cleanse Before Condemning.} Corruption does not always destroy the person or spirit beneath it.
{@b Honor the Dead.} Protect the spirits of the departed, for they represent what awaits beyond death.
{@b Leave No Evil.} When a spirit is truly beyond redemption, show it no mercy and leave none of its corruption behind.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain oath spells at the Paladin levels listed.

entries.name: Between Two Worlds
entries: Foxfire is not ordinary flame. It clings to spirits, and the stains left by supernatural corruption. Casting a cold light that harms what cannot be redeemed without consuming what remains innocent beneath it.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity
entries: When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

entries.name: Revealing Foxfire
entries: As an action, you present your holy symbol and wreathe one creature you can see within 30 feet of you in foxfire. You learn whether the creature is charmed, cursed, or possessed, though you don't learn the source of such an effect.

The creature must then make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@dice 2d8} fire damage, and for 1 minute it can't benefit from being invisible, shapechanged, or magically disguised. If it is shapechanged or magically disguised when it fails this saving throw, its true form is revealed for the duration.

entries.name: Cleanse the Spirit
entries: As an action, you present your holy symbol and choose one charmed, cursed, frightened, or possessed creature you can see within 30 feet of you. Choose one such effect afflicting the target. The target immediately repeats a saving throw against the effect, treating a roll on the d20 lower than your Paladin level as equal to your Paladin level. If the effect doesn't normally allow a saving throw, the target instead makes a Charisma saving throw against your Paladin spell save DC.
On a successful save, the chosen effect ends. If a creature caused that effect and is on the same plane of existence, foxfire briefly surrounds it and it takes {@dice 4d6} radiant damage.

subclassFeature.name: One-Tailed Fox
entries: Also at 3rd level, the kitsune spirits entrust you with a one-tailed spirit fox formed from foxfire. It is friendly to you and your companions and uses the Magical Fox stat block.
You determine its appearance, though it often resembles a canid surrounded by flames.

In combat, the fox shares your initiative count, but it takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its reaction independently, but the only action it takes on its turn is the Dodge action unless you use a bonus action to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its stat block or another action available to it. If you are incapacitated, the fox can take any action of its choice.
The fox can't willingly move more than 60 feet away from you. If it is farther than 60 feet from you at the end of a turn, it disappears and reappears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

If the fox is reduced to 0 hit points, it disappears, leaving behind only a fading flame. You can use an action and expend a spell slot of 1st level or higher to cause it to reappear within 5 feet of you with all its hit points restored. It also reappears with all its hit points when you finish a long rest.
{@creature Magical Fox|TwofellOathFoxfire}

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Cleansing
entries: Starting at 7th level, mote of spectral fire circles around you and wards nearby souls against supernatural corruption. You and friendly creatures within 10 feet of you have resistance to necrotic damage, have advantage on saving throws against being charmed or frightened, and can't be possessed while within the aura.
At 18th level, the range of this aura increases to 30 feet.

entries.name: Divided but united
entries: The Paladin and Fox can hold two places on the battlefield at once. Their auras soaring across the battlefield as which cannot be protected by the former, shall be covered by the companion. Carrying their will and protecting the soul beyond the Paladin's immediate reach.

subclassFeature.name: Three-Tailed Fox
entries: Also at 7th level, your spirit fox develops three tails and becomes a conduit for your divine power.

Whenever you use Divine Sense, its effect originates from both you and your fox. Your Aura of Cleansing also emanates from your fox. A creature within both instances of the aura gains its benefits only once.
The fox gains the following additional benefits.
{@b Carried Mercy.} When you use Lay on Hands, you can treat a creature within 5 feet of your fox as though it were within your reach.

{@b Lesser Smite.} When your fox hits a creature with Foxfire, you can expend a 1st-level spell slot to use Divine Smite through the attack. Foxfire counts as a melee weapon attack for the purpose of Divine Smite.
Your fox can also deliver the effects of any 1st-level Paladin spell with “Smite” in its name that is currently affecting you, treating its Foxfire as a melee weapon attack for that spell.

When you cast such a spell and choose for the fox to deliver it, you can use your action to command the fox to use Foxfire against a creature within its range. If the attack misses, the spell continues according to its normal duration.

subclassFeature.name: Six-Tailed Fox
entries: At 15th level, your spirit fox develops six tails. It gains a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover, and the damage of its Foxfire increases to {@dice 2d6} + your proficiency bonus.
Your fox can now use Divine Smite through Foxfire using a spell slot of 2nd level or lower. It can also deliver a Paladin spell of 2nd level or lower with “Smite” in its name.
When you cast such a spell and choose for the fox to deliver it, the fox can immediately use Foxfire as part of the same bonus action used to cast the spell.

subclassFeature.name: Purifying Smite
entries: Also at 15th level, you learn to strike through the cleansing flame carried by your companion.
Once on each of your turns, when you hit a creature illuminated by your fox's Foxfire with a melee weapon attack, the attack deals an additional {@dice 1d8} radiant damage.

You can then choose yourself or one friendly creature within your Aura of Cleansing. The chosen creature can immediately repeat a saving throw against one effect causing it to be charmed, frightened, cursed, or possessed.
If the effect doesn't normally allow a saving throw, the creature instead makes a Charisma saving throw against your Paladin spell save DC. On a successful save, the effect ends.

subclassFeature.name: Nine-Tailed Fox
entries: At 20th level, you and your companion can reveal the full power of your bond.
Your fox can now use Divine Smite through Foxfire using a spell slot of any level. It can also deliver any Paladin spell with “Smite” in its name.
As an action while your fox is manifested, you wreathe yourself in flames and cause the fox to assume a Large, nine-tailed form for 1 minute.

For the duration, the fox's flying speed increases to 60 feet, the damage of its Foxfire increases to {@dice 3d6} + your proficiency bonus, and both of you emit bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for an additional 30 feet.
The transformation grants the following additional benefits.

{@b Relentless Foxfire.} Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an attack, your fox can immediately use Foxfire against that creature without requiring an action or your bonus action.
{@b Ninefold Judgment.} As a bonus action, choose one creature within 60 feet of either you or your fox and apply one of the following effects:

items: {@b Cleanse.} The target regains hit points equal to {@dice 2d8} + your Charisma modifier, and you end one of the following conditions affecting it: blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, paralyzed, poisoned, or stunned. You can instead end one curse or possession affecting it. If the target is willing, you and your fox can each teleport to unoccupied spaces within 5 feet of it before or after cleansing it.

{@b Scorch.} The target must make a Charisma saving throw against your Paladin spell save DC. It takes {@dice 5d8} fire or radiant damage, chosen when you use this effect, on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Aerial
entries: {@b Amenity.} You can float up to 2 feet above a solid surface on which you could normally stand. While floating this way, nonmagical difficult terrain caused by the ground doesn't cost you extra movement, and you don't trigger effects activated by touching or stepping on the ground.
{@b Excursion.} You can cast {@spell feather fall|PHB} without expending a spell slot or providing material components.

optionalfeature.name: Astral
entries: {@b Amenity.} You can hold your breath for twice as long as normal. You also have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks made to identify portals, planar phenomena, and effects that alter gravity.
{@b Excursion.} As a bonus action, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

optionalfeature.name: Arctic
entries: {@b Amenity.} You suffer no ill effects from extreme cold. Additionally, nonmagical ice and snow don't cost you extra movement.

{@b Excursion.} When you deal your Local Specialty damage to a creature, you can force it to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, its speed becomes 0, and it can't take reactions until the start of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Coast
entries: {@b Amenity.} You gain proficiency with navigator's tools and water vehicles. Additionally, you can't become lost while traveling along a visible coastline except by magical means.

{@b Excursion.} When you deal your Local Specialty damage to a Large or smaller creature, you can force it to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, you push it up to 15 feet in a direction of your choice.

optionalfeature.name: Desert
entries: {@b Amenity.} You suffer no ill effects from extreme heat and have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks made to locate drinkable water. Additionally, your walking speed increases by 10 feet while moving on sand.
{@b Excursion.} When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll against you, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the roll.

optionalfeature.name: Fey
entries: {@b Amenity.} You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed}. Additionally, when you successfully forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would.

{@b Excursion.} When you deal your Local Specialty damage to a creature, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it is {@condition charmed} by you until the end of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Fiendish
entries: {@b Amenity.} You have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition frightened}, on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks made to discern deception during a verbal bargain, and on Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) checks made to discover deceptive language in a written contract.

{@b Excursion.} As an action, you cast {@spell command|PHB} at 1st level without expending a spell slot. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for this spell. When you cast the spell in this way, you gain resistance to fire damage for 1 minute.

optionalfeature.name: Forest
entries: {@b Amenity.} When you successfully forage, you find twice as much food as you normally would. You can also communicate simple ideas to Small or smaller beasts through sounds and gestures.

{@b Excursion.} As an action, choose yourself and up to a number of other willing creatures you can see within 30 feet of you equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one other creature). For 10 minutes, each target has advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks and can't be tracked by nonmagical means. The effect ends early on a target immediately after it makes an attack or casts a spell.

optionalfeature.name: Grassland
entries: {@b Amenity.} You can attempt to hide even when you are only lightly obscured by tall grass, heavy rain, falling snow, mist, or another natural phenomenon. Additionally, your walking speed increases by 5 feet.

{@b Excursion.} You can cast {@spell speak with animals|PHB} without expending a spell slot or providing material components. When you reach 11th level in this class, you can also cast {@spell speak with plants|PHB}.

optionalfeature.name: Haunted
entries: {@b Amenity.} After spending 1 minute focusing, you know whether an undead creature or cursed object is within 15 feet of you, though you don't learn its location or nature. This sense can't detect anything behind total cover.

{@b Excursion.} When you deal your Local Specialty damage to a creature, you can prevent it from regaining hit points until the start of your next turn. Until then, you also know its location while it is within 60 feet of you, even if it is {@condition invisible} or hidden.

optionalfeature.name: Holy
entries: {@b Amenity.} You have advantage on Intelligence ({@skill History}) and Intelligence ({@skill Religion}) checks concerning religions, religious practices, holy sites, divine rites, and celestials.

{@b Excursion.} As a bonus action, choose yourself or one creature you can see within 30 feet. The chosen creature regains hit points equal to {@dice 2d6} + your Wisdom modifier. The healing increases to {@dice 2d8} when you reach 11th level in this class.

optionalfeature.name: Mountain
entries: {@b Amenity.} {@b Highland Hiker.} You gain a climbing speed equal to your walking speed minus 10 feet, to a minimum of 5 feet. You are also acclimated to high altitude, including elevations above 20,000 feet.

{@b Excursion.} {@b Immovable Summit.} As a bonus action, you steady yourself for 1 minute. For the duration, you can't be knocked {@condition prone} or moved against your will while you aren't {@condition incapacitated}.

optionalfeature.name: Ruins
entries: {@b Amenity.} Your passive Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) score increases by 5 when used to notice traps, secret doors, or unstable structures.

{@b Excursion.} When you or another creature within 5 feet of you is hit by an attack, you can use your reaction to grant the target a +5 bonus to its AC until the start of its next turn, including against the triggering attack. The attack might miss as a result.

optionalfeature.name: Shadow
entries: {@b Amenity.} You gain {@sense darkvision} out to a range of 60 feet. If you already have darkvision, its range increases by 30 feet.
{@b Excursion.} As a bonus action, you become {@condition invisible} for 1 minute. The invisibility ends early immediately after you make an attack or cast a spell.

optionalfeature.name: Swamp
entries: {@b Amenity.} You have resistance to poison damage and advantage on saving throws against being {@condition poisoned}. Additionally, nonmagical mud and shallow water don't cost you extra movement.

{@b Excursion.} When you deal your Local Specialty damage to a Large or smaller creature standing on the ground, you can force it to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, the creature is {@condition restrained} for 1 minute. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

optionalfeature.name: Underdark
entries: {@b Amenity.} You always know your approximate depth below the surface. Additionally, you can cause yourself or an object you are carrying to shed dim light in a 10-foot radius. You can produce or extinguish this light using a bonus action.
{@b Excursion.} As a bonus action, you gain {@sense blindsight} out to a range of 10 feet for 1 minute. The range increases to 15 feet when you reach 11th level in this class.

optionalfeature.name: Underwater
entries: {@b Amenity.} You gain a swimming speed equal to your walking speed, and you can hold your breath for twice as long as normal.
{@b Excursion.} When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes cold or piercing damage, you can use your reaction to reduce that damage by {@dice 1d10} + your ranger level.

optionalfeature.name: Urban
entries: {@b Amenity.} You have advantage on ability checks made to interpret maps, obtain directions, or secure accommodations in a settlement. When you pay for accommodations, their quality is treated as one lifestyle category higher, to a maximum of Wealthy.

{@b Excursion.} As a bonus action, choose one willing creature within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you. That creature can use its reaction to move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. It then has advantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Volcanic
entries: {@b Amenity.} You have resistance to fire damage caused by environmental hazards, such as lava or steam. You can also attempt to hide while lightly obscured by ash, smoke, or steam.

{@b Excursion.} When you deal your Local Specialty damage to a creature, you can cause flames to erupt around it. Each other creature within 5 feet of the target must make a Dexterity saving throw. A creature takes {@dice 2d6} fire damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one. The damage increases to {@dice 2d8} when you reach 11th level in this class.

optionalfeature.name: Wasteland
entries: {@b Amenity.} You have advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks made to scavenge, and Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) checks to find hidden objects and treasure.

{@b Excursion.} As a bonus action, you gain temporary hit points equal to your ranger level + your Wisdom modifier. While you have any of these temporary hit points, difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement.

optionalfeature.name: Saline Augmentation

item: A simple or martial weapon or a pair of gloves (requires attunement)

entries: The item has 6 charges. When the wearer makes a Strength check or a Strength saving throw, it can expend 1 charge to add your Intelligence modifier to the roll. If the wearer would be knocked {@condition prone}, it can use its reaction to expend 1 charge to avoid being knocked prone. The item regains {@dice 1d6} expended charges daily at dawn.

{@b Infused (Salt).} While the item contains a Salt atom, the wearer can use a bonus action to expend it and become unnaturally dense for 1 minute. For the duration, it counts as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift; it has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws; and it can’t be knocked {@condition prone}. The effect ends early if the wearer is {@condition incapacitated}.

optionalfeature.name: Pneumatic Soles
entries: While wearing these boots, a creature can teleport up to 15 feet as a bonus action to an unoccupied space it can see. The destination must be a space the creature occupied at some point during the current turn.

{@b Infused (Air).} While the boots contain an Air atom, the wearer can expend it as a reaction when hit by a ranged attack, interposing a violent crosswind. The wearer gains a bonus to its AC equal to your proficiency bonus against the triggering attack, potentially causing it to miss, and against all other ranged attacks until the start of its next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Telluric Aegis

item: A suit of armor or a shield

entries: The wearer gains a +1 bonus to Armor Class while wearing the armor or wielding the shield. This bonus increases to +2 when you reach 10th level in this class.

{@b Infused (Earth).} While the item contains an Earth atom, the wearer can expend it as a reaction when it takes bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing damage. The wearer gains resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage until the start of its next turn, including against the triggering damage.

optionalfeature.name: Incendiary Channel

item: A simple or martial weapon or an artificer spellcasting focus (requires attunement)

entries: If the infused item is a weapon, it grants a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. If it is an artificer spellcasting focus, it grants a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls made with artificer spells cast through it, and those attacks ignore half cover. Either bonus increases to +2 when you reach 10th level in this class.

{@b Infused (Fire).} While the item contains a Fire atom, the wielder can expend it when it damages a creature to release a searing flash. The damaged creature and each other creature of the wielder’s choice within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your artificer spell save DC or be {@condition blinded} until the start of the wielder’s next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Aqueous Adaptation

item: A suit of armor, cloak, or shield (requires attunement)

entries: The wearer has resistance to cold damage. It can also breathe underwater and gains a swimming speed equal to its walking speed.

{@b Infused (Water).} While the item contains a Water atom, the wearer can use a bonus action to expend it and briefly assume a fluid state. It immediately ends the {@condition grappled} and {@condition restrained} conditions on itself. Until the end of the turn, it can move through the space of any creature and through openings as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing, but it can’t end this movement in an occupied space.

optionalfeature.name: Vitae Reservoir

item: An amulet, brooch, or suit of armor (requires attunement)

entries: The wearer stabilizes whenever it is dying at the start of its turn. In addition, whenever the wearer rolls a Hit Die to regain hit points, double the number of hit points it restores.

{@b Infused (Vitae).} While the item contains a Vitae atom, the wearer can expend it when it fails an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw to reroll the saving throw, potentially turning the failure into a success. It must use the new roll. If the effect would possess the wearer or transform its body, it makes this reroll with advantage.

optionalfeature.name: Mors Needle

item: A simple or martial weapon or an artificer spellcasting focus (requires attunement)

entries: If the infused item is a weapon, it grants a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it. If it is an artificer spellcasting focus, it grants a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls made with artificer spells cast through it, and those attacks ignore half cover.

{@b Infused (Mors).} While the item contains a Mors atom, the wielder can expend it when it damages a creature with the infused weapon, or with an artificer spell cast using the infused focus, to expose that creature’s mortality. The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your artificer spell save DC or become vulnerable to the next instance of damage it takes before the start of the wielder’s next turn. A creature immune to necrotic damage is immune to this effect.

optionalfeature.name: Quintessential Matrix

item: A suit of armor, amulet, or spellcasting focus (requires attunement)

entries: The bearer gains a +1 bonus to Armor Class and saving throws.
{@b Infused (Quintessence).} While the item contains a Quintessence atom, the bonus to Armor Class and saving throws is a +2.

The bearer can use an action to expend it and cast {@spell wall of force|phb} from the item without expending a spell slot or providing material components. Intelligence is the spellcasting ability for this spell, and the bearer must concentrate on it as normal.

optionalfeature.name: Mercurial Actuator

item: A helmet, pair of gloves, or pair of boots (requires attunement)

entries: The wearer has advantage on initiative rolls. In addition, it can’t be surprised, provided it isn’t {@condition incapacitated}.

{@b Infused (Quicksilver).} While the item contains a Quicksilver atom, the wearer can use a bonus action to expend it and accelerate its reflexes for 1 minute. For the duration, its speed increases by 10 feet, it gains a +2 bonus to Armor Class, it has advantage on Dexterity saving throws, and it can take the Dash, Disengage, Search, or Use an Object action as a bonus action. The effect ends early if the wearer is {@condition incapacitated}.

optionalfeature.name: Annotation
entries: When the spell affects one or more hostile creatures, choose one of them. Until the end of the next turn of the creature that cast the spell, the first time you or an ally hits the chosen creature with an attack, that attack deals extra force damage equal to your Intelligence modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Application
entries: When the spell affects you or an ally, that creature can immediately stand up without using any of its movement or move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.

optionalfeature.name: Conversion
entries: {@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell deals acid, cold, fire, force, lightning, poison, or thunder damage.
When you or an ally casts the spell, that creature can change its damage type to acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, or thunder.

optionalfeature.name: Correction
entries: {@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell requires a spell attack roll.
When a spell attack made as part of the spell misses, you or the ally that cast the spell can reroll the attack against the same target. The new roll must be used.

optionalfeature.name: Emphasis
entries: {@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell deals damage, restores hit points, or grants temporary hit points.

When the spell deals damage to, restores hit points to, or grants temporary hit points to one or more creatures, choose one of those creatures. Increase the damage dealt, hit points restored, or temporary hit points granted to that creature by your Intelligence modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Precision
entries: A creature gains no benefit from half cover against the spell and gains only the benefit of half cover from three-quarters cover against the spell.

optionalfeature.name: Reach
entries: Increase the spell's range by 30 feet. If it has a range of touch, its range becomes 15 feet instead. This Revision has no effect on a spell with a range of Self.

optionalfeature.name: Safety
entries: {@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell affects an area.
Choose one creature in the spell's area. That creature is unaffected by the spell.

optionalfeature.name: Continuity
entries: {@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell requires concentration.
When you or an ally casts the spell, the creature concentrating on it adds your Intelligence modifier to the first Constitution saving throw it makes to maintain concentration on the spell.

optionalfeature.name: Controlled
entries: {@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell rolls damage or restores hit points.
When you or an ally casts the spell, that creature can reroll a number of the spell's damage or healing dice up to your Intelligence modifier. It must use the new rolls.

optionalfeature.name: Distillation
entries: {@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell has a duration of at least 1 minute and no longer than 1 hour.
Double the spell's duration, to a maximum of 2 hours. If the spell requires concentration, it still requires concentration.

optionalfeature.name: Expansion
entries: {@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell creates an area.
Increase the radius of the spell's area by 5 feet, the length of a cone or line by 10 feet, or each dimension of a cube or square by 5 feet.

optionalfeature.name: Guided
entries: {@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell has a range of touch.

When you or an ally casts the spell, choose one willing creature that the creature casting the spell can see within 60 feet of it. The chosen creature can use its reaction to deliver the spell to one creature within its reach. The spell still uses your spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus.

optionalfeature.name: Residual Effect
entries: {@b Insight Cost.} 2 Insights.
{@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell forces a saving throw.

Choose one creature that succeeds on its first saving throw against the spell. Until the start of the next turn of the creature that cast the spell, the chosen creature's speed is reduced by 10 feet, and it can't take reactions.

optionalfeature.name: Reformulation
entries: If all spell attacks made as part of the spell miss or every target succeeds on its first saving throw against it, you gain 1 Insight.

optionalfeature.name: Adaptation
entries: {@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell deals damage.
Damage dealt by the spell ignores resistance to that damage. Immunity is unaffected.

optionalfeature.name: Multiplicity Casting
entries: {@b Insight Cost.} 2 Insights.
{@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell can target a single creature, doesn't have a range of Self, and can't target an object.

When you or an ally casts the spell and targets only one creature with it, choose a second creature within 30 feet of the original target that is also an eligible target for the spell. The spell targets the chosen creature in addition to the original target. If the spell requires concentration, you or the ally that cast the spell concentrates on a single spell that affects both targets.

optionalfeature.name: Persistence
entries: {@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell can force the same creature to make more than one saving throw over its duration.

When a creature succeeds on a saving throw against the spell after previously failing a saving throw against it, you or the ally that cast the spell can force the creature to reroll the saving throw. It must use the new roll. A creature can be affected by this Revision only once per casting.

optionalfeature.name: Multiple Spell Application
entries: {@b Insight Cost.} 3 Insights.
{@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell has a range of Self and affects only the creature casting it.
When you or an ally casts the spell, choose one willing creature within 30 feet of you or that ally. The spell also affects the chosen creature for its duration.

optionalfeature.name: Spell Transfer
entries: {@b Insight Cost.} 2 Insights.
{@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell has a duration longer than instantaneous, can target a willing creature, and targets only one creature.

As a bonus action while the spell lasts, the creature affected by the spell can touch another willing creature. The spell ends on the first creature and affects the second creature for the remainder of its duration.

optionalfeature.name: Shocking Rebuttal
entries: {@b Insight Cost.} 2 Insights.
{@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell forces a saving throw.

Choose one creature that succeeds on its first saving throw against the spell. That creature has disadvantage on the next attack roll or ability check it makes before the start of the next turn of the creature that cast the spell.

optionalfeature.name: Dual Demonstration
entries: {@b Insight Cost.} 2 Insights.
{@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell creates an area.

When you or an ally casts the spell, choose one willing creature within 60 feet of the creature that cast it and visible to that creature. The spell creates a second, identical area originating from the chosen creature's space.

optionalfeature.name: Perfectly Supported Citation
entries: {@b Insight Cost.} 3 Insights.

The spell can't be countered by {@spell counterspell|PHB}. If the spell requires a spell attack roll, you or the ally that cast it has advantage on one spell attack roll made as part of the spell. If the spell instead forces a saving throw, choose one creature affected by it. That creature has disadvantage on its first saving throw against the spell. Once you apply this Revision, you can't apply it again until you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Reliabla Replicable Result
entries: {@b Insight Cost.} 3 Insights.
{@b Requirement.} You cast your Thesis Spell using a spell slot.
Before the end of your next turn, you can cast the spell one additional time at its lowest level without expending a spell slot.

optionalfeature.name: Infallible Arcane Formula
entries: {@b Insight Cost.} 3 Insights.
{@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell requires a spell attack roll or forces a saving throw.

If the spell requires a spell attack roll, choose one spell attack made as part of it. Treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10 for that attack. If the spell instead forces a saving throw, choose one creature affected by it. That creature can't benefit from advantage on its first saving throw against the spell.

optionalfeature.name: Lasting Proof
entries: {@b Insight Cost.} 2 Insights.
{@b Requirement.} Your Thesis Spell has a duration of at least 1 minute and requires concentration.
The spell no longer requires concentration, and its duration becomes 1 minute.

entries.name: Performance Rights
entries: Your patron grants you a song, melody, chant, dance routine, battle hymn, or fan call that becomes magical when performed. Every pact song is considered registered property of your patron.
When you choose this Pact Boon at 3rd level, you learn two pact songs of your choice. You learn one additional pact song of your choice at 7th level, and one more at 12th level.
A remix is an enhanced version of a pact song. You don’t learn a remix as part of this Pact Boon, but eldritch invocations and other features can grant access to one.

entries.name: Pact Song
entries: As a bonus action, you can begin one pact song you know. A pact song lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are {@condition incapacitated} or if you begin another pact song.
Your pact song creates an aura centered on you, as shown in the Pact Song Aura table.

When you begin a pact song, choose a number of willing creatures within the aura, up to your Charisma modifier (min. 1). Each chosen creature gains hype equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus.

You can begin a pact song a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest. If you have no uses remaining, you can expend a warlock spell slot to begin a pact song.
Hype gained from a pact song lasts until the song ends or until the hype is depleted.

entries.name: Fan Benefits
entries: A fan benefits from your pact song only while it has hype from you, is within your pact song aura, and can see or hear you.
Leaving the aura doesn’t remove this hype, but the fan can’t benefit from the pact song until it is within your pact song aura again and can see or hear you.

entries.name: Remix Tracks
entries: A remix improves one pact song you know. You can benefit from a pact song’s remix only while that pact song is active.
Learning a pact song doesn’t automatically grant its remix. The {@optfeature Remixed Debut|TwofellIdolCompendium} eldritch invocation is the most common way to learn one.

entries.name: One Song at a Time
entries: Unless a feature says otherwise, a creature can benefit from only one pact song at a time. If it would benefit from a different pact song, it chooses which one to keep.

entries.name: Pact Songs and Other Patrons
entries: Pact of the Song is available to warlocks of any patron. A warlock whose patron is not the Idol Agency still uses the hype and fan rules in this document for hype granted by pact songs, but gains no other Idol Agency feature.

The performance should reflect the patron or their nature. An Archfey warlock might dance through glamour and dreamlike music, a Celestial warlock might sing hymns and inspire allies, a Fiend warlock might play rock, and a Great Old One warlock might produce harmonies that should not fit mortal conventions. Fathomless warlocks may perform sea shanties, Genie warlocks reciting fables and poetry, Hexblade warlocks executing weapon forms, and Undead or Undying warlocks may sing dirges and epics.
A pact song does not have to be literal music. It can be a dance, poem, prayer, speech, martial forms, weapon drills, fan call or other repeated performance. Its rules remain unchanged.

optionalfeature.name: Killer Melody
entries: The first time on each of its turns that a fan hits with an attack, the attack deals extra psychic damage equal to your Charisma modifier (min. 1).

{@b Remix.} The extra damage becomes {@damage 1d4} + your Charisma modifier (min. 1). The fan can lose hype up to its Charisma modifier (min. 1) to increase the extra damage by the amount of hype lost.

optionalfeature.name: Patch Me Up!
entries: At the start of each fan‘s turn, if that fan has at least 1 hit point and no more than half its hit point maximum, it loses any amount of hype up to your Charisma modifier (min. 1), then regains hit points equal to the hype lost.
This song can’t restore a creature to more than half its hit point maximum.
{@b Remix.} The maximum hype it can lose this way becomes twice your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus (min. 1).

optionalfeature.name: Glassheart
entries: Fans gain a +1 bonus to AC.
{@b Remix.} This bonus increases to +2.

optionalfeature.name: Step-Step-Go
entries: Once on each of its turns, a fan can use a bonus action to move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.
{@b Remix.} This movement increases to 15 feet, and the fan ignores difficult terrain during this movement.

optionalfeature.name: Lucky Signal
entries: Once per round, when a fan makes an ability check or saving throw, it can roll {@dice 1d4} and add the number rolled to the result. A creature can’t add this die and a die from the {@spell bless} spell to the same roll.
The fan can roll the die before or after making the d20 roll, but before the DM says whether the roll succeeds or fails.
{@b Remix.} The die becomes a {@dice d6}.

optionalfeature.name: Aim Towards the Sky
entries: Once per round, when a fan makes an attack roll, it can roll {@dice 1d4} and add the number rolled to the result. A creature can’t add this die and a die from the {@spell bless} spell to the same roll.
The fan can roll the die before or after making the d20 roll, but before the DM says whether the attack hits or misses.
{@b Remix.} The die becomes a {@dice d6}.

optionalfeature.name: Crowd Battery
entries: At the start of each of your turns, choose one fan within your pact song aura. That fan gains hype equal to your proficiency bonus.
Hype gained from this pact song disappears when the pact song ends.
{@b Remix.} You can choose two different fans within your pact song aura instead of one.

optionalfeature.name: Beat of the Heart
entries: Fans have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition blinded} or {@condition deafened}.
When a fan makes a Constitution saving throw to maintain concentration, it adds your proficiency bonus to the roll.
{@b Remix.} When a fan fails a Constitution saving throw to maintain concentration, it can choose to succeed instead.
Once a fan succeeds in this way, it can’t do so again until it finishes a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Call Me, Answer Me
entries: When a fan takes the {@action Help} action to aid another fan, the helped fan gains hype equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus (min. 1).
The helped fan can also roll {@dice 1d4} and add the number rolled to the first attack roll or ability check it makes before the end of its next turn.
{@b Remix.} Once before the start of each of your turns, one fan can take the {@action Help} action as a bonus action, but only to aid another fan. The bonus die becomes a {@dice d6}.

optionalfeature.name: Overdrive
entries: Fans gain a 10-foot bonus to speed.
When a fan takes the {@action Dash} or {@action Disengage} action, it gains hype equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus (min. 1).

{@b Remix.} A fan can take the {@action Dash} or {@action Disengage} action as a bonus action. Once a creature benefits from this remix, it can’t benefit from this remix again until it finishes a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Center of My World
entries: When you start this song, choose one fan as the Focus.
When the Focus hits with an attack on its turn, it can lose 1 hype. If it does, the attack deals extra psychic or radiant damage, the Focus’s choice, equal to your Charisma modifier (min. 1).
At the start of each of your turns while the song lasts, you can choose a different fan within your pact song aura to be the Focus.
{@b Remix.} When the Focus deals this extra damage, it can lose 2 hype instead of 1. If it does, the extra damage becomes {@damage 1d6} + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus (min. 1).

optionalfeature.name: Vocal Spark
entries: Once per turn, when you cast a warlock cantrip and target only one creature with it, one fan within your pact song aura can use its reaction to empower the spell.
If the spell hits or the target fails its saving throw, the spell deals extra psychic damage equal to your Charisma modifier.
{@b Remix.} The extra damage becomes {@damage 1d6} + your Charisma modifier, and the fan that used its reaction gains hype equal to your proficiency bonus.

optionalfeature.name: Patchwork Halo
entries: When a fan within your pact song aura takes damage, another fan within your pact song aura that can see or hear the damaged fan can use its reaction to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d10} + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus. Only one fan can use its reaction for each instance of damage.
{@b Remix.} Once before the start of each of your turns, after a fan reduces damage with this pact song, both fans gain hype equal to your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Last Stand
entries: The first time a fan would be reduced to 0 hit points while this song is active, the fan is reduced to 1 hit point instead.
Once a creature benefits from this song, it can’t benefit from this song again until it finishes a long rest.
{@b Remix.} When a fan is reduced to 1 hit point by this song, it also gains hype equal to your warlock level.

optionalfeature.name: Ghostlight Parade
entries: Fans have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition frightened}.
While a fan is within your pact song aura, invisible creatures don’t have advantage on attack rolls against that fan as a result of being invisible.
{@b Remix.} Fans can see invisible creatures within 10 feet of them, provided the invisible creature is also within your pact song aura.

optionalfeature.name: Smile Until Dawn
entries: When a fan starts its turn with no more than half its hit point maximum, it has advantage on the first attack roll or saving throw it makes before the start of its next turn.
{@b Remix.} The first time the fan hits with an attack before the start of its next turn, it adds your Charisma modifier to the attack’s damage roll.

optionalfeature.name: Syndrome
entries: Once before the start of each of your turns, when a fan within your pact song aura misses with an attack roll or fails an ability check or saving throw, another fan within your pact song aura can use its reaction to harmonize with it.
The triggering fan rolls {@dice 1d4} and adds the number rolled to the result, potentially turning the miss or failure into a hit or success.
{@b Remix.} The die becomes a {@dice d6}. If the triggering roll hits or succeeds after adding this die, both fans gain hype equal to your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: No Bad Takes
entries: Once on each of its turns, when a fan fails an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, it can lose hype equal to your proficiency bonus to reroll the d20. It must use the new roll.
{@b Remix.} The fan loses only 1 hype when it rerolls the d20 in this way.

optionalfeature.name: Only Love Me~
entries: At the start of each fan‘s turn, if that fan is {@condition blinded}, {@condition charmed}, {@condition deafened}, {@condition frightened}, or {@condition poisoned}, it can immediately repeat one saving throw against one of those effects, ending that effect on itself on a success.
A fan can repeat a saving throw in this way only once per turn.
{@b Remix.} When a fan succeeds on a saving throw granted by this pact song, it gains hype equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus.

optionalfeature.name: Sold-Out
entries: Fans have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to avoid being {@condition grappled}, {@condition restrained}, knocked {@condition prone}, or moved against their will.
Once on each of its turns, when a fan escapes a grapple, stands up from prone, or ends the restrained condition on itself, it can move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks.
{@b Remix.} This movement increases to 20 feet. After the fan moves in this way, it gains hype equal to your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Drop Like a Meteor
entries: Once on each of its turns, when a fan hits a creature with an attack, the fan can force the target to make a Wisdom saving throw against your warlock spell save DC.
On a failed save, the target’s speed is halved, it can’t make opportunity attacks and it has disadvantage on the next attack roll it makes before the start of the fan‘s next turn.
{@b Remix.} On a failed save, the target also takes psychic damage equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus.

optionalfeature.name: Long-Distance Cue
entries: When you cast {@spell guidance} on one of your fans, the spell’s range becomes 60 feet.
The target must be able to see or hear you.

optionalfeature.name: Battle Cue
entries: When you cast {@spell guidance}, you can alter the spell so that it doesn’t require concentration and its die can be added to one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw made before the spell ends. The spell ends immediately after the die is rolled.
If the die causes the roll to hit or succeed, the target gains hype equal to your proficiency bonus.
You can alter {@spell guidance} in this way a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Quick Cue
entries: You can cast {@spell guidance} as a bonus action, the spell has a range of 30 feet, and the target must be able to see or hear you.
You can cast {@spell guidance} in this way a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Remixed Debut
entries: Choose one pact song you know. You learn that song’s remix.
Whenever you gain a warlock level, you can replace the chosen remix with the remix of another pact song you know.
You can choose this invocation more than once, choosing a different pact song each time.

optionalfeature.name: Extended Discography
entries: You learn one additional pact song of your choice.
You can choose this invocation more than once, choosing a different pact song each time.

optionalfeature.name: Opening Number
entries: When you roll initiative, you can immediately begin a pact song you know without using an action. Beginning a pact song in this way expends a use as normal.
Once you use this invocation, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Feel it in the Heart!
entries: The radius of your pact song aura increases by 15 feet.
Your fans don’t need to see you to benefit from your pact song, provided they can hear you.

optionalfeature.name: Extended Encore
entries: When your pact song would end after lasting for 1 minute, you can extend it for 1 additional minute.
Once you extend a pact song this way, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Stereo Audio
entries: When you begin a pact song by expending a warlock spell slot, you can choose two pact songs you know instead of one. Both songs are active at the same time.
For the duration, a fan can benefit from both active pact songs at the same time. This overrides One Song at a Time for these two songs.
Once you use this invocation, you can’t do so again until you finish a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Music Player
entries: When you finish a long rest, you can create a Tiny magical device and store one pact song you know within it. The stored song remains until you finish another long rest or create a new Music Player.

A willing creature holding or wearing the device can use a bonus action to activate it. The creature gains hype equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus, and for 1 minute it gains the benefits of the stored pact song as if it were one of your fans within your pact song aura and could see and hear you. The effect ends early if the creature is {@condition incapacitated}, can no longer hear the device or ends it as a bonus action.

The device affects only the activating creature and doesn’t create an aura. If the song requires you to choose a fan when it begins, the activating creature is the chosen fan. An effect of the stored song that requires another fan can’t be used or triggered.
The stored song counts as one of your pact songs for the activating creature, including for the purpose of One Song at a Time.
Once the device is activated, it can’t be activated again until you finish a long rest. You can have only one Music Player at a time. If you create another, the previous one becomes nonmagical.

optionalfeature.name: Premium Subscription
entries: Your Music Player has 3 charges, and activating it expends 1 charge. These charges replace its normal once-per-long-rest activation. The device can’t be activated while its stored pact song is already active, and it regains all expended charges when you finish a long rest.
When a creature activates the device, the hype it gains equals your warlock level + your Charisma modifier, instead of the normal amount.
If you know the remix of the stored pact song, the activating creature can also gain the remix‘s benefit for the duration.

optionalfeature.name: Protect Me!
entries: When you are hit by an attack, one of your fans within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you can use its reaction and lose 5 hype to protect you.

The fan teleports to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you and becomes the target of the triggering attack instead. The attack hits the fan regardless of its AC, and the attack’s damage and other effects are resolved against that fan.
Once a fan protects you in this way, it can’t do so again until it finishes a long rest.
This invocation can be used a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

condition.name: Toxin
entries: Whenever one or more creatures take poison or necrotic damage from you, you can give one Toxin counter to each of those creatures. A creature can have a maximum number of your Toxin counters equal to your proficiency bonus.
A creature’s speed is reduced by 5 feet for each of your Toxin counters it has. While a creature has a number of your Toxin counters equal to your proficiency bonus, it is also {@condition poisoned}.

At the end of each of its turns, a creature with one or more of your Toxin counters can make a Constitution saving throw against your druid spell save DC. On a successful save, it removes one Toxin counter. All your Toxin counters on a creature disappear if it has not gained one of your Toxin counters for 1 minute.

Toxin is a magical effect. A creature immune to the {@condition poisoned} condition can still accumulate Toxin counters and suffer their reduction to its speed, but it can’t become poisoned by this feature.

trait.name: Brood Segments
entries: Each Spiderling in the Brood has a separate hit point segment equal to 5 + twice your proficiency bonus. Damage dealt to the Brood is applied to one segment at a time, with excess damage carrying over to the next segment. When a segment is reduced to 0 hit points, its Spiderling dies, reducing the Brood’s number of Spiderlings and its hit point maximum accordingly.
A new Spiderling added to the Brood adds one undamaged segment to it. The Brood can’t regain hit points by any other means.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The Brood can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Swarm
entries: The Brood can occupy another creature’s space and vice versa, and it can move through any opening large enough for a Tiny Spiderling.

trait.name: Telepathic Brood
entries: While the Brood is within 120 feet of you, you can communicate telepathically with each Spiderling within it. The Spiderlings can telepathically communicate simple emotions, images, and anything they perceive through their senses.

trait.name: Web Walker
entries: The Brood ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

action.name: Bites
entries: {@i Melee Spell Attack:} your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. {@h} {@damage 1d4} piercing damage for each Spiderling currently in the Brood, plus poison damage equal to your proficiency bonus.

trait.name: Spider Climb
entries: The Broodmother Ascendant can climb difficult surfaces, including upside down on ceilings, without needing to make an ability check.

trait.name: Web Sense
entries: While in contact with a web, the Broodmother Ascendant knows the exact location of any other creature in contact with the same web.

trait.name: Web Walker
entries: The Broodmother Ascendant ignores movement restrictions caused by webbing.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The Broodmother Ascendant makes two Foreleg attacks.

action.name: Foreleg
entries: {@i Melee Weapon Attack:} your spell attack modifier to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h} 8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) piercing damage plus 3 ({@damage 1d6}) poison damage.

action.name: Venomous Barb
entries: {@i Ranged Weapon Attack:} your spell attack modifier to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. {@h} 8 ({@damage 1d8 + 4}) piercing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) poison damage.

action.name: Web {@recharge 5}
entries: {@i Ranged Weapon Attack:} your spell attack modifier to hit, range 30/60 ft., one Large or smaller creature. {@h} The creature is {@condition restrained} by webbing. As an action, the restrained creature can make a Strength check against your druid spell save DC, escaping on a success. The webbing can also be attacked and destroyed (AC 10; 15 hit points; vulnerability to fire damage; immunity to poison and psychic damage).

entries: Your alignment.

trait.name: Skills

entries: {@i Ranged Spell Attack:} your spell attack modifier to hit, range 60 ft., one target. {@i Hit:} {@dice 1d6} + your proficiency bonus fire or radiant damage, chosen when the attack hits. The target sheds dim light in a 5-foot radius and can't benefit from being invisible until the start of the fox's next turn. The fox has advantage on this attack against Undead.

data.name: Introduction
entries: The Idol Compendium is a collection of player options and campaign material themed around idols, magical performers, and the industries that shape them. Its centerpiece is the Idol Agency Otherworldly Patron, a support-focused warlock subclass that keeps allies healthy and inspired with hype, alongside Pact of the Song, a pact boon that lets any warlock lead allies through supernatural singing, dancing, and performance. The compendium also includes performer backgrounds, feats, equipment, magic items, and tools for creating an Agency of your own.

entries.name: The Agency
entries: The Agency may be a supernatural entertainment company, fey talent label, celestial production house, cursed idol office, eldritch management corporation or soul-draining industry with impeccable branding.
It promises to nurture your hidden talent, make your dreams come true and bloom you into an unforgettable performer. In return, it expects obedience, loyalty and a part of your soul.

entries.name: Using This Compendium
entries: The Idol Agency patron and Pact of the Song are the mechanical center of this supplement, but neither is required to use its other player options. The backgrounds, feats, equipment, and most magic items can be used by characters of any class.

entries.name: Player and DM Material
entries: Pages 3-21 contain player-facing rules and options. Pages 22-28 provide compatibility guidance and campaign material, including a complete fey Agency.

data.name: The Idol Agency
entries: Otherworldly Patron for Warlocks
Support Your Fans - Build Hype - Survive the Show

entries.name: Performer Tools in Play
entries: These trinkets can remain decorative or become minor adventure hooks. A future ticket might identify a time traveler, an event yet to occur, or someone from another dimension. A censored page might complete a ritual song, while a mysterious key might lead into an Agency’s private backstage halls. Like the trinkets found in Ravenloft, they are intended to remain strange, suggestive, and not always fully explained.

entries.name: Hype
entries: Hype is a special kind of temporary hit points granted by your Idol Agency features, pact songs, or spells given or modified by this subclass.
When a creature that already has hype from you gains hype from you, the new hype is added to the old hype, instead of replacing it.

entries.name: Fan
entries: A creature with hype from you is one of your fans. When a creature has no hype from you, it stops being your fan.
A creature’s maximum hype from you equals twice your warlock level + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus (min. 1).

entries.name: Hype and Temporary Hit Points
entries: Hype functions as temporary hit points except where its rules say otherwise. It does not restore consciousness, and any damage left after hype is depleted carries over to hit points.
Hype granted by different warlocks does not add together. A creature chooses which warlock’s hype to keep, just as it chooses between different sources of temporary hit points.

entries.name: Fans Are Not Charmed
entries: Being your fan is a rules term. It does not make a creature admire you, obey you or regard you as friendly. A hostile willing creature could technically become a fan, although most hype features require willing targets.

entries.name: Pact Songs Are Not Spells
entries: A pact song is magical but is not a spell. It cannot be counterspelled or dispelled unless a feature specifically says otherwise, and it does not require concentration. It still ends if you are {@condition incapacitated} or begin another pact song.
A fan must satisfy the song’s requirements to gain its benefits. A fan that can neither see nor hear you cannot benefit unless a feature says otherwise.

entries.name: Multiclass Characters
entries: Whenever this document refers to your warlock level, use only your levels in the warlock class. Use your warlock spell save DC for a pact song or invocation that calls for a saving throw.

entries.name: Adjudicating Performances
entries: A character does not need to make a Performance check every time a pact song begins. The magic comes from the pact, not from proving artistic quality. Use ability checks only when the surrounding fiction creates uncertainty, such as winning over an audience, hiding a coded message in a dance or maintaining a mundane performance during a disaster.

entries.name: Instruments and Silence
entries: A pact song can be a dance, gesture or visual routine, so magical silence does not automatically end it. Silence prevents fans from hearing it, and darkness, blindness or blocked sight may prevent them from seeing it. The performer decides the song’s usual form when learning it, but can present it differently when the fiction reasonably allows.

entries.name: Suggested Content Boundaries
entries: Agency stories can involve exploitation, overwork, coercive contracts and loss of identity. Before using those themes heavily, establish which elements belong in the game, which should remain off-screen and which should not appear.

data.name: Creating an Agency
entries: Building an Idol Company for Your Campaign

entries.name: Step 1: Choose the Public Face
entries: {@b What the World Sees}
Decide how the Agency presents itself. It might be a glamorous talent company, magical academy, philanthropic arts foundation, adventuring guild, religious choir, or fashionable lifestyle brand.
The public face determines how easily the Agency attracts recruits, earns trust, and conceals harmful practices behind respectable language and polished presentation.
It is useful to create one or more NPCs who serve as the face of the company, such as its CEO, star idol, recruiters, or trainers.

entries.name: Step 2: Choose the Core Promise
entries: {@b What Recruits Believe They Will Gain}

Every Agency sells its recruits something. Choose what it promises: fame, beauty, belonging, power, escape from obscurity, reinvention, or the chance to become the person someone always wished to be. An Agency can make one central promise or several related promises.
This promise is the emotional foundation of the Agency. It explains why people would willingly accept its help and endure the hardships that come with such work.

entries.name: Step 3: Choose the True Nature
entries: {@b What Exists Behind the Brand}

Determine who or what truly controls the Agency. It might be an eldritch being, an Archfey, a celestial chorus, an infernal board of directors, a sentient contract, a ghostly producer, or an ordinary company supported by mundane or supernatural investors.
The Agency’s true nature explains its impossible resources, magical contracts, unusual performers, and the internal rules that must be followed.

entries.name: Step 4: Choose the Price of Success
entries: {@b What the Agency Takes}

Decide what performers surrender in exchange for their success. The price might be as ordinary as time and effort or as supernatural as obedience, loyalty, memories, names, emotions, years of life, or part of a soul. Any of these can serve as fuel for the Agency.
The price establishes the central danger of the Agency. It should make success desirable while ensuring that achieving it creates a meaningful personal cost.

entries.name: Step 5: Choose the Internal Structure
entries: {@b How the Company Operates}

Choose two or three departments or systems that define daily life within the Agency. Common examples include scouting, training, publicity, legal enforcement, costume design, magical development, security, fan relations.

This gives the Agency a recognizable culture, creating staff roles, locations, terminology, and recurring situations that characters can investigate or exploit. An Agency can instead operate as a deliberate black box whose methods remain unknown even when it produces reliable results.

entries.name: Step 6: Choose the Method of Control
entries: {@b How Performers Are Kept Compliant}

Determine how the Agency keeps its idols compliant. It might rely on debt, blackmail, magical contracts, public image pressure, mind control, selective information, isolation, surveillance, or the threat of immediate replacement. Its performers might instead remain through loyalty, professional pride, or genuine care from their employers. Not every Agency rules through fear or manipulates its talent.
This distinguishes the Agency from an ordinary demanding employer. Its method of control should be visible enough for the characters to understand, resist, or eventually undermine.

entries.name: Step 7: Connect the Party
entries: {@b Why Every Character Is Involved}

Tie one or more members of the party to the Agency when possible. One character might be a performer, another a bodyguard, and a third a friend trying to rescue someone inside or simply a fan of the Agency’s music.

If it is the focus of the campaign, the Agency should create a shared conflict rather than a story that matters to only one character. If it is secondary, it can provide respite from the main plot or reinforce its themes.

data.name: Lavender Reverie Entertainment
entries: Example Fey Agency

Lavender Reverie Entertainment is a magical-idol company styled around elegant witches, floral arrangements, and polished modern branding. It promises to turn every recruit into “the idol of their dreams.” The promise is genuine, but LRE modifies those dreams to fit its own agenda, stripping away individuality to manufacture perfect idols.

entries.name: Alvilda
entries: {@b Faerie Lady of Dreams}
Alvilda is a poised and refined faerie noble who holds dominion over dreams.

She founded the company to help her daughter achieve her ambitions. She remained after discovering how delicate youthful dreams can be, and how entertaining it is to reshape them into her vision of what an idol should be.

entries.caption: LRE CEO
rows: CEO and Faerie Lady of Dreams
An Archfey who rules over dreams and longs to understand her own
Lavender, moonlight, witch hats, ribbons, charms, stars, and accessories
Help anyone become the idol they have always dreamed of being

entries: {@i “Your old self was only the first draft. Let me show you the version that shines.”}

entries.name: Public Face
entries: Lavender Reverie presents itself as an exclusive label for aspiring idols. Its performers combine song, dance, illusion magic, and witch-themed stagecraft with carefully managed public personas.

Its releases are structured like mysteries. Lyrics contain hidden messages and collectible merchandise reveals fragments of fictional dream lore. Fans are encouraged to decode the group’s story together. To outsiders, the Agency appears unusual but prestigious.

entries.name: Core Promise
entries: Lavender Reverie promises to uncover the recruit’s ideal self: the idol they imagined becoming, or the magical heroine hidden beneath fear and inexperience.

Alvilda believes that most people are trapped inside incomplete versions of themselves. She sees no cruelty in removing the memories, relationships, or values that prevent someone from reaching their more beautiful form.

entries.name: True Nature
entries: Lavender Reverie is an Archfey-owned entertainment company that draws power from unrealized possibility and the emotional weight of dreams.

Contracts are both legal agreements and binding scripts. Rehearsals continue during sleep. Transformation sequences double as rituals. A debut is the moment when the public persona becomes real enough to begin competing with the person underneath it.

The Agency does not erase an identity all at once. It changes portions of it over time. A performer might remember their childhood but not the name they used during it. They might recognize a former friend without remembering why that person was important. They might retain an old ambition while believing the Agency was responsible for giving it to them.

entries.name: Price of Success
entries: Lavender Reverie’s contracts commonly claim one or more of the following:

items: The performer’s old name, which gradually disappears from memories and written records.
The right to “improve” dreams.
Ownership of the performer’s stage name, recorded voice, costume, and magical transformation.
The right to create an understudy capable of inheriting the same public identity.
A portion of the performer’s unrealized dreams, which Alvilda stores and reshapes for later projects.

entries: Most performers do not realize how much has changed until they attempt to describe who they were before joining the Agency, only to find that they lack the words to speak about their old selves.

entries.name: Internal Structure
entries: Lavender Reverie resembles a fashionable entertainment company, but its departments combine corporate management with fey dreamcraft.
{@b Dream Scouting.} Recruiters observe the dreams of gifted, lonely, dissatisfied, or ambitious people. Prospects often receive invitations tailored to their desires.
{@b Image Curation.} Stylists, composers, and minor faeries let each recruit choose from a collection of magical motifs, costumes, and signature colors, but the Agency assigns the stage name.
{@b Sleep Rehearsal.} Performers continue rehearsing inside their dreams. Training can feel like a full night of work even when only a few waking hours pass.
{@b Narrative Development.} Each group receives an unfolding mystery told through songs, performances, interviews, and merchandise. The members themselves may not know the solution.
{@b Retention and Recovery.} Performers who resist their assigned identity are offered rest, meaning an extended hiatus from which they return noticeably different.
{@b Understudy Development.} The Agency quietly trains replacements capable of inheriting the role, visual motif, voice, and even stage name. No one is ever safe.

entries.name: Method of Control
entries: Lavender Reverie relies on dependence and partial identity rewrite rather than direct physical violence.

A performer’s new identity is reinforced by magical costumes, dreams, public recognition, fan expectations, and staff who use only the approved stage name. Their old life becomes increasingly difficult to access or remember.
Personal doubts are classified as nightmares. Their exhaustion is deemed as failure and resistance to transformation. Their objections, reframed as fear of becoming one’s true self.
The Agency also uses some… less than savory methods:

items: Moral debt created by providing aspiring idols with training, housing, fame, and food to the needy.
Dream surveillance presented as wellness checks, suppressing dissents when detected.
Controlled scandals used to discipline uncooperative performers.
Replacement performers prepared before the original has been dismissed.

entries.name: Immediate Pressure
entries: Lavender Reverie’s flagship witch-idol unit is preparing a major comeback whose lore centers on reclaiming dreams from an unnamed darkness.

One member has begun hearing their old name in dreams, where it accuses them of abandoning the person they once were. Another remembers a childhood that clashes with what they know of themselves. Their newest song contains lyrics that appear to reverse part of the Agency’s binding process.
At the same time, Alvilda’s daughter has begun questioning whether the company is helping its performers or replacing them with more convenient versions of themselves.
Alvilda finds the conflict fascinating. She has not decided whether to suppress it, encourage it, or turn it into the group’s next mystery.

entries.name: Signature Themes
entries: Lavender Reverie’s performers are styled as modern magical girls and elegant witches, using hats, ribbons, brooches, wands, and charms. Their songs explore diverse subjects but frequently return to identity, memory, and growth through hardship. Groups move with unnatural synchronization, while fans gather in forums to unravel mysteries by decoding lyrics, tracing recurring symbols, and comparing collectible dream fragments.

entries.name: Running the Agency
entries: For a lighter game, the Agency can be a pushy magical label with suspicious but mostly harmless branding. For a darker game, make it akin to a black company: everything is polished, everyone is replaceable and every kindness creates a debt.

entries.name: The Agency as a Patron
entries: The Agency should create adventures, temptations, and difficult choices. It should not be used as an excuse to routinely overrule a player character’s decisions or diminish them. Even a soul contract is most useful when the character can resist, reinterpret, expose, or eventually break it.
Other characters can also interact with the Agency. It does not need to be exclusively the warlock’s problem.
