background.name: Amateur Performer
entries: You sang in taverns, danced at festivals, performed street magic, acted in local plays or chased any open stage that would give you the chance. You have talent and ambition, but no established reputation, and a dream of one day making it big.
{@b Skill Proficiencies:} Performance, Persuasion
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} One type of musical instrument, makeup kit
{@b Equipment:} A musical instrument of your choice, a makeup kit, a performance costume, 10 autograph cards, a handbill advertising one of your performances, and a pouch containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Local Act
entries: Due to your skills and experience asking around, you can usually find a modest venue willing to let you perform, provided entertainment is welcome there. While you perform regularly, you can earn enough to support yourself at a modest lifestyle. The venue’s workers and other local performers are generally willing to share rumors and gossip about the audience, patrons and recent trouble with you.

entries.caption: Personality Traits
rows: I turn almost any task into a performance.
I remember every person who applauded me on my first show.
I practice introductions before meeting people.
I pretend not to care when someone ignores my work.
I collect cheap decorations and make them look expensive.
I eagerly trade techniques with other performers.
When on stage, I am a different person.
I always have a new act that is almost ready, but never finish it.

entries.caption: Ideals
rows: Expression. Art should say what ordinary words cannot. (Chaotic)
Joy. A good performance should leave people happier. (Good)
Recognition. I have worked too hard to remain unknown. (Any)
Tradition. The old songs and stories must be preserved. (Lawful)
Freedom. No patron or audience owns my voice. (Chaotic)
Influence. Attention is power, and I intend to earn it by any means. (Evil)

entries.caption: Bonds
rows: The first person who paid to see me perform still has my loyalty.
My old troupe is the closest thing I have to a family.
I carry an unfinished work dedicated to someone I lost.
I promised my home that I would return famous.
A rival and I pushed each other to become better.
I perform under a name given to me by someone important.

entries.caption: Flaws
rows: I cannot resist an audience, even when performing is a bad idea.
I spend money as though my next show will be a success.
I become bitter when someone else receives attention I wanted.
I exaggerate my reputation until I believe my own stories.
I treat useful criticism as a personal attack.
I will accept almost any challenge to prove that I have talent.

background.name: Agency Trainee
entries: You spent months or years enduring strict schedules, lessons, evaluations, and rules. You might have been preparing for a debut, working toward an audition or simply hoping not to be cut from the program.
{@b Skill Proficiencies:} Acrobatics, Insight
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} One type of musical instrument, makeup kit
{@b Equipment:} A set of training clothes, a makeup kit, a musical instrument of your choice, an old rehearsal schedule or unsigned contract, an agency meal packet, and a pouch containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Rehearsal Discipline
entries: You recognize the routines, terminology and working habits of professional performers. In a settlement with an entertainment industry, you can usually identify instructors, agents and low-level staff by looking at them. Other trainees and working performers tend to treat you as a peer unless you give them reason not to.

entries.caption: Personality Traits
rows: I rehearse simple tasks until I can do them perfectly.
I instinctively find the focal point in any room.
I apologize before anyone has explained what went wrong.
I smile through discomfort and never complain.
I track food and sleep as though both will be evaluated.
I can fall asleep almost anywhere when given permission.
I put other people’s work before my own.
I become intensely competitive when someone doubts my training.

entries.caption: Ideals
rows: Discipline. Talent means nothing without work. (Lawful)
Teamwork. Nothing succeeds because of one person alone. (Good)
Perfection. Mistakes are weaknesses that can be trained away. (Any)
Escape. I will never again let an institution define my worth. (Chaotic)
Status. I endured suffering, others should too. (Evil)
Responsibility. I must protect those who are still trapped inside. (Good)

entries.caption: Bonds
rows: A former trainer believed in me when no one else did.
I still exchange secret letters with a friend who was left behind.
Another trainee took the blame for my worst mistake.
My unsigned debut contract is proof that I almost made it.
I owe my health or freedom to a staff member who helped me.
I promised a former partner that one of us would reach the stage.

entries.caption: Flaws
rows: I hide injuries and exhaustion until I collapse.
I assume every kindness should be repaid.
I need permission before resting, even when no one is in charge.
I compare myself to everyone around me.
I find it difficult to tell where my persona ends.
I obey confident instructions without questioning them.

background.name: Backstage Hand
entries: You worked behind the curtain on important productions as a dresser, carpenter, prop handler, makeup artist, runner, or general assistant. You learned that a smooth performance is usually held together by people the audience never notices.
{@b Skill Proficiencies:} Investigation, Sleight of hand
{@b Tool Proficiencies:} Makeup kit, one type of artisan’s tools
{@b Equipment:} A makeup kit, a set of artisan’s tools with which you are proficient, common clothes, a battered backstage pass, 10 feet of string, a piece of chalk, and a pouch containing 10 gp

entries.name: Feature: Backstage Access
entries: You know how theaters, halls, and stages are organized. You can usually identify staff entrances, storage rooms, rigging access, and other practical routes through a performance venue, as well as how to blend in when uninvited. When a production is in town, you can generally secure work for yourself in exchange for helping backstage.

entries.caption: Personality Traits
rows: I notice when backstage has been messed with.
I solve problems before anyone sees them.
I know exactly how long five minutes is.
I keep spare pins, string, chalk and snacks for emergencies.
I know better than anyone who says a job will be easy.
I speak more bluntly to famous people than they expect.
I collect gossip but sometimes make my own.
I feel uncomfortable when people thank me directly.

entries.caption: Ideals
rows: Reliability. The work will be finished because I said I would. (Lawful)
Safety. No performance is worth a worker’s life. (Good)
Craft. The invisible details matter most. (Any)
Solidarity. On a team everyone should protect each other. (Good)
Access. A locked door is an invitation to learn what is behind it. (Chaotic)
Leverage. Secrets are the only payment that never loses value. (Evil)

entries.caption: Bonds
rows: My old crew remembers me, no matter how far away I am.
I carry a tool that belonged to a worker who never came home.
A performer once protected me from my boss, and I owe them.
I know a scandal that could destroy an important person.
I planned a perfect show and dream of seeing it performed.
Someone is still using the hidden route I created through an old venue.

entries.caption: Flaws
rows: I assume every leader is hiding something.
I take tools, keys and documents because they might be useful.
I cannot leave a faulty mechanism alone, even when time is short.
I resent performers who ignore the people supporting them.
I accept dangerous work and don’t admit I cannot handle it.
I use private information as leverage.

feat.name: Trained Performer
entries: You have developed your talent through lessons, rehearsal and repeated public performances. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in the {@skill Performance} skill. If you are already proficient in it, your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses Performance.
You gain proficiency with one musical instrument or a makeup kit.
You have advantage on ability checks made to continue a performance through distractions, heckling, or poor weather.

feat.name: Quick-Change Artist
entries: You can alter your presentation with exceptional speed. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency with a makeup kit. When you make an ability check using a makeup kit, you can use Dexterity in place of the ability normally used for the check.
You can prepare a disguise using a makeup kit over the course of 10 minutes. Thereafter, you can don or remove that disguise as an action.
When a creature you can see makes a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check to see through a disguise you created, you can use your reaction to impose disadvantage on the check.

feat.name: Stage Presence
entries: Your practiced voice and bearing naturally draw attention. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your voice can be heard clearly at twice the distance it normally could, provided you are not whispering.

After speaking or performing before one or more creatures for at least 1 minute, you have advantage on the next Charisma ({@skill Performance}) or Charisma ({@skill Persuasion}) check you make to influence those creatures within the next 10 minutes.

entries: A creature that cannot see or hear you, or that was hostile throughout the performance, is unaffected by this benefit.

feat.name: Vocal Impressionist
entries: You have trained your ear and voice to reproduce what you hear. You gain the following benefits:

items: You can mimic the speech of another person or the sounds made by a creature. You must have heard the person or creature for at least 1 minute. A listener can determine that the sound is imitated with a successful Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check contested by your Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check.
After studying a written speech, song or script for 10 minutes, you can recite up to 100 words from it without error for the next 24 hours.

feat.name: Public Persona
entries: You have built a practiced identity that is easier to remember than the person beneath it. You gain the following benefits:

items: Choose a stage name, title and recognizable mannerism. You have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Deception}) and Charisma ({@skill Performance}) checks made to present yourself as this persona.

A creature that knows you only through your persona does not automatically recognize you while you are not using it. When a creature attempts to recognize your true self, make a Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check contested by its Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check. The creature has disadvantage on its check.

feat.name: Ensemble Player
entries: You excel at making another person look their best.

When you take the {@action Help} action to aid a creature with an ability check, the creature also gains temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus. Once a creature gains temporary hit points from this feat, it can’t do so again until it finishes a short or long rest.
In addition, you can take the {@action Help} action as a bonus action. You can do so a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

feat.name: Perfect Timing
entries: You know when a small cue can prevent a mistake and how to deliver it to prevent it.

When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll or ability check, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to the roll. You can use this reaction after seeing the roll but before the DM says whether it succeeds or fails.
You can use this feat a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

feat.name: Opening Act
entries: You know how to establish momentum before anyone else can seize the room. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you roll initiative, choose yourself or one creature within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you. The chosen creature gains temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier.

entries: You can grant temporary hit points in this way a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.

feat.name: Media Trained
entries: You know how to survive questioning, rumors and hostile interactions. You gain the following benefits:

items: You gain proficiency in {@skill Insight} or {@skill Persuasion}. If you already have proficiency in the chosen skill, your proficiency bonus is doubled for checks you make with it.

After a creature speaks with you for at least 1 minute, you can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check contested by its Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check. On a success, you learn whether it is primarily trying to inform, embarrass, provoke or recruit you. You do not learn whether any individual statement said during conversation is true.

feat.name: Choreographed Partners
entries: You have practiced moving around your allies without breaking their rhythm. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you move through the space of a willing creature, that space does not count as difficult terrain for you.

When a willing creature you can see ends its turn within 5 feet of you, you can use your reaction to allow both you and that creature to move up to 10 feet. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.

During a short or long rest, you can rehearse with one willing creature. Until the start of your next short or long rest, each of you has advantage on the first ability check you make to perform, dance, create or maintain a disguise, or coordinate with the other creature.

feat.name: Unshakable Smile
entries: You have been trained to maintain your composure under pressure. You gain the following benefits:

items: You have advantage on saving throws against effects that would force you to speak, laugh, cry or otherwise display an involuntary emotion.
Other creatures have disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) checks made to determine your current emotional state from your expression or voice.

item.name: Agency Badge
entries: This marked badge identifies a performer, trainee or worker as belonging to a particular company. A convincing false badge can be created with a {@item forgery kit|PHB} if the maker has seen an authentic one before.

item.name: Agency Meal Packet
entries: Each packet contains only half the food a creature needs for one day and no water. The food keeps for one year, tastes faintly medicinal, and includes propaganda for an organization.

item.name: Autograph Cards (20)
entries: These decorated cards provide a convenient surface for signatures, messages, illustrations or minor magical marks or sigils. A signed card can serve as proof that its holder met the person represented, though signatures can be forged.

item.name: Campaign Fan
entries: This folding fan bears a symbol or set of colors. Creatures who have rehearsed together can use visible fan motions to communicate simple instructions over long distances such as cheer, advance, retreat, wait, look or begin. The signal can be understood at up to 150 feet by a creature that can see it clearly.

item.name: Costume, Performance
entries: A performance costume is designed to be seen and appreciated, with a distinct style chosen for its performer. It can serve as fine clothes where its dramatic appearance is appropriate, but it is readily recognized as stagewear under close inspection.

item.name: Costume Repair Kit
entries: This kit contains thread, wire, pins, adhesive, spare fasteners and patches. You can repair visible damage to one costume or set of clothing during a short or long rest.

item.name: Cue Cards (20)
entries: A creature that spends 10 minutes rehearsing from these cards can memorize a speech or sequence of up to 40 words. It can repeat that sequence without error for the next 8 hours.

item.name: Glowstick
entries: As an action, you can snap and shake this alchemical rod, causing it to shed bright light of various colors in a 5-foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet for 4 hours. Once activated, it cannot be extinguished or reused.

item.name: Makeup Kit
entries: A makeup kit is a {@item disguise kit|PHB} presented as cosmetics, brushes, adhesives and stage prosthetics. It follows all the rules for a disguise kit, and proficiency with either kit applies to checks made with the other.

item.name: Microphone, Acoustic
entries: This handheld cone or resonant crystal carries the user’s voice. While speaking through it, your voice can be heard clearly at twice the distance it normally could, though it does not overcome magical silence.

item.name: Publicity Portraits (10)
entries: A creature that studies an accurate portrait for 1 minute has advantage on the next Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check it makes within 24 hours to recognize the depicted subject by sight. An inaccurate or outdated portrait grants no advantage.

item.name: Rehearsal Markers (10)
entries: This set contains brightly colored tape, chalk and numbered tokens used to mark positions. A creature that spends 1 minute placing them has advantage on the next Intelligence check it makes within 1 hour to recall the positions of creatures, props or objects in the marked area.

item.name: Stage-Smoke Pellet
entries: As an action, you can throw the pellet at a point on the ground within 30 feet. It creates a 5-foot cube of smoke that is lightly obscured until the end of your next turn. The pellet is then destroyed.

item.name: Animated Photocard
entries: This glossy card displays a flattering animated portrait of the creature whose name is written on its back. When a creature finishes a long rest while holding the card, it can replace the name with that of another creature it can see.
The named creature can touch the card to change the portrait’s pose and expression.

While holding the card, a creature can roll {@dice 1d4} and add the number rolled to a Charisma ({@skill Performance}) check it makes to introduce, praise or promote the named creature. Once this property is used, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

item.name: Applause in a Bottle
entries: When this tiny bottle is opened, it produces up to 1 minute of applause, cheers, boos or the chirping of a cricket chosen by the opener. The sound can be heard from 100 feet away and is obviously artificial to a creature that examines it closely. Once used, the bottle refills at the next dawn.

item.name: Centerpiece Crown
entries: While wearing this delicate crown, you have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Performance}) checks made as part of a group performance.

When a willing creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction to add your Charisma modifier to the roll, potentially changing the result. You can use this reaction after seeing the roll, but before the DM says whether it succeeds or fails.
After the roll is resolved, you can exchange places with the creature. You and the creature teleport to each other’s spaces. Once this property is used, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

item.name: Contract Pen
entries: This black pen never runs out of ink.

When a creature signs its true name with the pen, the creature holding the signed object can choose a blank sheet of paper within 1 mile whose location it knows. An exact copy of the signed object appears on that sheet, including any writing, seals and marks present when it was signed.
Once this property is used, it can’t be used again until the next dawn.

item.name: Costume of a Thousand Roles
entries: As a bonus action while wearing this costume, you can alter its appearance and cause it to resemble any set of clothing you have seen.
You can cast {@spell disguise self} from the costume at will.

In addition, you can cast {@spell alter self} from it without expending a spell slot. Once you cast {@spell alter self} in this way, you can’t do so again until the next dawn. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

item.name: Echoing Microphone
entries: You can use this microphone as a spellcasting focus. It has 3 charges.

When you cast a spell that targets only a willing creature and has a range other than Self, you can expend 1 charge to double the spell’s range. If the spell restores hit points or grants temporary hit points, the target also gains additional temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.
The microphone regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn.

item.name: Encore Blade
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
When you attack with this weapon, you can use your Charisma modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, for the attack and damage rolls.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with the rapier, you can choose another creature within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you. The chosen creature gains temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.
item.reqAttune: by a creature with a Charisma score of 13 or higher

item.name: Finale Baton
entries: You can use this baton as a spellcasting focus. While holding it, you gain a +1 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells.

The baton has 5 charges. When a creature you can see within 60 feet misses with an attack roll or fails an ability check or saving throw, you can use your reaction and expend 1 charge to roll {@dice 1d6} and add the number rolled to the triggering roll, potentially causing it to hit or succeed. If the roll hits or succeeds, the creature also gains temporary hit points equal to your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus.
The baton regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the last charge, roll a {@dice d20}. On a 1, the baton plays a final triumphant chord and becomes nonmagical.
item.reqAttune: by a bard, cleric, paladin or warlock

item.name: Glowstick of Encouragement
entries: This glowstick can be extinguished or relit as a bonus action and never runs out of light.
As a bonus action, you can wave it toward one creature you can see within 30 feet. The creature gains 1 temporary hit point.

item.name: Harmony Blades
entries: These paired magic daggers count as one magic item for the purpose of attunement. You are proficient with them while attuned, and you gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with them.
When you attack with either dagger, you can use your Charisma modifier, instead of Strength or Dexterity, for the attack and damage rolls.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with one of the daggers, choose one willing creature within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you. The first time that creature hits the same target before the start of your next turn, its attack deals an extra {@damage 1d8} psychic damage.

item.name: Idol’s Emergency Hairpin
entries: While wearing this decorated pin, your hair, ribbons and costume accessories remain arranged despite wind, rain and movement. As an action, you can cause one tear, stain or scuff on your clothing to become invisible for 1 hour.

item.name: Makeup of the Unfaltering Smile
entries: This elegant makeup never runs or smears. While wearing it, magical and mundane attempts to determine your emotional state from your face automatically fail.

When you fail a saving throw against being {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you do so, you cannot remove the makeup until the next dawn, and you gain one level of {@condition exhaustion} when the effect that caused the saving throw ends. The curse is revealed only after this property is used.

item.name: Manager’s Clipboard
entries: This clipboard always displays the names of creatures you have formally assigned to a task. As an action, you can write the names of up to six willing creatures on it. Their names remain until you erase them or write a new list.

When you take the {@action Help} action to aid a listed creature with an ability check, you can do so from up to 60 feet away if it can see or hear you and your assistance could reasonably guide the task. You can use this property a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining all uses daily at dawn.

item.name: Mascot Head of Joy
entries: While wearing this oversized mascot head, your voice is muffled and your face cannot be seen. You have advantage on Charisma ({@skill Performance}) checks made to entertain through broad movement, pantomime or physical comedy, but disadvantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or hearing.

The head has 3 charges. You can expend 1 charge as an action to cast {@spell silent image}, but the illusion must include the mascot in question. It regains {@dice 1d3} expended charges daily at dawn.

item.name: Noncompete Choker
entries: While wearing this jeweled choker, you gain a +1 bonus to Charisma ability checks and saving throws.

When you receive payment, shelter or magical aid from a creature other than the person who gave you the choker, you must succeed on a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw or be unable to knowingly act against the giver’s interests for 24 hours. The creature that gave you the choker is aware when you fail this save. Removing the choker does not end this effect until {@spell remove curse} is cast on you.

item.name: Producer’s Earpiece
entries: When you finish a short or long rest while wearing this earpiece, you can designate a number of willing creatures equal to your proficiency bonus. Until you use this property again, you and each designated creature can communicate telepathically with one another while within 120 feet, provided every participant is wearing or carrying an earpiece of their own.

The earpiece has 3 charges. When a designated creature you can see starts moving within 60 feet of you, you can use your reaction and expend 1 charge to guide it. The creature can move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
The earpiece regains all expended charges daily at dawn.

item.name: Redacted Contract Seal
entries: Pressing this seal to a written document causes up to 100 words of your choice to become invisible. The words remain present and legally part of the document. They can be seen with {@spell see invisibility}, revealed by {@spell dispel magic} against {@dc 15}, or restored when the seal is pressed to the document again.

The seal can conceal words in this way once per dawn. A creature that spends 10 minutes examining an affected document can make a {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check, noticing suspicious gaps or spacing on a success but not revealing the hidden words.

item.name: Regalia of the Unforgettable Star
entries: You gain a +3 bonus to AC while wearing this armor.
You can’t be {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened}, and your clothing, hair and carried decorations remain clean and arranged despite ordinary weather, movement and combat.

When you roll initiative, choose a number of creatures within 30 feet of you that can see or hear you, up to your proficiency bonus. Each chosen creature gains temporary hit points equal to 10 + your Charisma modifier.

As an action, you can begin a Grand Entrance. Each willing creature of your choice within 30 feet can immediately move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. Each creature that moves in this way has advantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes before the end of its next turn.
Once you use Grand Entrance, you can’t use it again until the next dawn.
item.reqAttune: by a creature with a Charisma score of 15 or higher or proficiency in Performance

item.name: Resonant Stage Gem
entries: This thumb-sized crystal pulses in time with nearby music. While a pact song is active, you can use a bonus action to place or throw the gem to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet. The gem has AC 15, 10 hit points and immunity to poison and psychic damage.

While you are within 60 feet of the gem, you can choose for your pact song aura to be centered on the gem instead of you. You can change the center of the aura between yourself and the gem as a bonus action. The pact song still ends if you are {@condition incapacitated}, and the gem cannot maintain the song without you.
If the gem is reduced to 0 hit points, it becomes inert until the next dawn. You can recall an intact gem to your hand as a bonus action while it is within 60 feet.
item.reqAttune: by a warlock with the Pact of the Song feature

item.name: Shoes of the Marked Stage
entries: These polished shoes leave faint glowing marks that vanish after 1 minute. You can suppress or resume this effect as a bonus action.

Your walking speed increases by 5 feet. In addition, standing up costs you only 5 feet of movement, and you have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) checks made to maintain your footing during a performance or on a constructed stage.

item.name: Spotlight Coat
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to AC while wearing this armor.
As a bonus action, you can alter the coat’s colors, decorations and apparent material.
When a creature misses you with an attack, you can use your reaction to move up to 10 feet without provoking opportunity attacks from that creature.

item.name: Spotlight Knife
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
As a bonus action, you can cause the dagger to shed bright light in a 10-foot radius and dim light for an additional 10 feet, or extinguish the light.

When you hit a creature while you have advantage on the attack roll, you can cause it to glow until the start of your next turn. During that time, the creature can’t benefit from being invisible, and the next attack roll made against it by a creature other than you has advantage.
Once this property is used, it can’t be used again until you finish a short or long rest.

item.name: Stageguard Leathers
entries: While wearing this armor, standing up from {@condition prone} costs you only 5 feet of movement.
You also have advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to avoid being knocked {@condition prone} or moved against your will while standing on a constructed floor, platform or stage.

item.name: Understudy Costume
entries: As a bonus action while wearing this costume, you can alter its colors, decorations and apparent style. The costume cannot resemble armor or equipment that it does not possess.
After observing another creature’s clothing for at least 1 minute, you can cause the costume to imitate that clothing.

table.name: Performer Trinkets
table.caption: Performer Trinkets
rows: A fan letter addressed to a stage name you have never used.
A cracked glowstick that glows faintly when people are singing.
A rehearsal schedule containing one date in the future.
A costume jewel that shines in the dark.
A wooden microphone carved with the names of forgotten performers.
A sealed envelope containing your own unsigned resignation.
A tiny mascot doll whose expression changes when no one is looking.
A ribbon awarded for a competition you do not remember entering.
A makeup mirror that reflects stage lighting even in darkness.
A ticket for a sold-out performance in a city that does not exist.
A songbook with most of its words illegible or censored.
A brass key that fits a dressing-room door in every theater.
A timecard stamped with hours you never worked.
A contract whose last page is signed by you.
A publicity portrait in which one member of the group is blurred out.
A bottle labeled “bath water” of unknown origin.
An agency badge that grows scorchingly hot whenever you consider quitting.
A ranking chart that always places you one position below someone else.
A broken earpiece that occasionally whispers a song.
A bouquet that remains fresh but loses one flower each dawn.

table.name: Lavender Reverie Party Connections
table.caption: Party Connections
rows: A party member performs under a Lavender Reverie contract.
A friend or relative no longer remembers the name they had before joining.
A party member worked for the Agency and discovered its dream corrections.
A party member once auditioned and still sees Alvilda during their sleep.
The party was hired to find a missing idol whose scheduled appearances have continued.
A party member knows Alvilda’s daughter and has been drawn into her conflict with the company.

table.name: Agency Representatives
table.caption: Agency Representatives
rows: A faceless producer whose smile appears only in reflections.
A mascot familiar with soft fur and a blank stare.
A celestial choreographer who calls pain “correction.”
A fey manager who remembers every promise you made as a child.
A cursed mirror that insists on showing your flaws.
A ghostly senior idol who insists they are “still under contract.”
A cheerful clerk who speaks entirely with impersonal statements.
A former adventurer who now treats performers like a military unit.

table.name: Agency Departments
table.caption: Agency Departments
rows: Legacy management for retired or deceased talent

table.name: Contract Clauses
table.caption: Contract Clauses
rows: You must never respond to your previous name.
You must smile before patrons, nobles and paying guests.
You must maintain a perfect public image.
You must win the hearts of new fans wherever you perform.
You must never speak of the previous idol.
You must answer any summons sealed with the Agency’s mark.
Your stage name, costume and recorded voice belong to the Agency.
Time spent unconscious, imprisoned or dead does not pause the contract.

table.name: Industry Omens
table.caption: Industry Omens
rows: Your autograph writes itself when you touch the page.
Your dressing-room door locks whenever you consider quitting.
A fan thanks you for a performance you do not remember giving.
Your old name fades from letters, records and family ledgers.
There is a room backstage with a mannequin that eerily resembles you.
Your shadow keeps shifting after you stop moving.
A ranking board changes whenever you feel proud.
Your costume is repaired and cleaned each night, impeccable and ready to be worn.

table.name: Exploitative Practices
table.caption: Exploitative Practices
rows: Mandatory unpaid rehearsals described as opportunities.
Injuries are concealed until the show ends.
Trainees compete for food, beds or access to healing.
Every gift is recorded as debt against future earnings.
Staff are ordered to create rumors about their own performers.
Retired talent must train replacements who use their identities.
Fan complaints are magically transferred into the performer’s dreams.
The Agency controls who may speak to a performer without supervision.

table.name: Current Scandal
table.caption: Current Scandal
rows: A supposedly live performance used an illusory duplicate.
A beloved idol has been missing for months while scheduled appearances continue.
The Agency has been buying its own merchandise to falsify popularity.
A rival’s breakdown was deliberately engineered.
A trainee died during a ritual described as coaching.
Fan meetings are being used to locate magically compatible sacrifices.
Several performers share the same memories of childhood.
The Agency’s most famous song contains a hidden command word.

table.name: Escape Clauses
table.caption: Escape Clauses
rows: Complete one final performance before an impossible audience.
Find the original copy of the contract and break it.
Convince another willing creature to inherit the stage name.
Make the Agency publicly admit that it broke its own rules.
Recover every fragment of your true name.
Become more famous than the Agency itself.
Fulfill a forgotten promise made by the Agency’s founder.
End the contract in the place where it was first signed.

table.name: Rival Acts and Groups
table.caption: Rival Acts and Groups
rows: A perfectly synchronized group that never speaks offstage.
A former friend who accepted the debut you rejected.
A cheerful independent troupe that the Agency wants destroyed.
An undead act performing under their lost names.
A noble-sponsored performer protected from ordinary consequences.
A masked soloist who claims to be the original you.
A monster presented as a harmless magical mascot.
A rival Agency whose working conditions are somehow worse.

table.name: Public Personas
table.caption: Public Personas
rows: The reformed villain with a suspiciously clean history

table.name: What the Agency Wants Now
table.caption: What the Agency Wants Now
rows: Recruit a specific adventurer as new talent.
Recover stolen recordings from a rival.
Perform in a dangerous region to prove the Agency’s reach.
Turn a recent disaster into favorable publicity.
Wear a new item that is clearly cursed.
Replace a missing performer without telling the audience.
Deliver a sealed contract without reading it.
